stories.Headline: OpenAI adds computer-use agents and over 20 plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 16, 2026, that it is expanding ChatGPT for Healthcare with advances in computer-use agents, improved trusted clinical search, and more than 20 new healthcare plugins. The computer-use agents can navigate existing healthcare software by reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications. OpenAI said it is working with healthcare organizations including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together information care teams need. The announcement was reported by HCI Innovation Group on Nov. 17, 2026, in an article by Pietje Kobus-McAllister. The updates are intended to help healthcare organizations reduce time spent navigating disconnected software and streamline workflows from referral management and documentation to insurance verification and care coordination.

The computer-use agents include access controls and audit logs, and organizations can set which applications agents can access and which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models. In a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations, and in over 1300 reviews rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness. All of the more than 20 new plugins are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow.

The plugin list includes Aiva, Amion, Assort Health, Availity, Extend, Elation Health, Ferry, IMO Health, MCP Server, Infinitus, Relay, K Health, Luma Health, Metriport, Notable Integration Specs, Oracle HDI Overview, PenguinAI Medical Coding, Photon, Redox, Stedi, Subsalt, Trizetto, Turquoise, and UpToDate Expert AI. Elation Health's read-only beta plugin lets primary care practice managers use ChatGPT to identify patients scheduled for the following day who have gaps in insurance, registration, or contact information, and staff receive a list of issues to review and address in Elation's electronic health record before patients arrive. Kyna Fong, co-founder and CEO of Elation Health, said AI earns its place in primary care by helping the people who use it, and that the company earns it by being thoughtful about its use, maintaining control, and using it to make stronger systems. Infinitus is bringing its Relay agents into ChatGPT to support benefits verification and prior authorization workflows, and users can initiate a benefits verification, check the status of a prior authorization and identify next steps, or submit batch requests using a spreadsheet. Ankit Jain, CEO of Infinitus, said the next chapter of AI in healthcare won't be defined by how much information it can surface but by what it can actually accomplish.

The Elation beta is initially available to a limited group of Elation practices, and the company said the approach is designed to keep administrative work with AI while leaving clinical decisions and patient outreach under the control of practice teams. Relay is available to existing Infinitus customers using ChatGPT for Healthcare, and the integration is designed to let healthcare and life sciences organizations access Infinitus agents without leaving ChatGPT. Jain said healthcare is full of complex, interconnected workflows that require more than answering questions, requiring navigating systems, taking action, and following through, and that bringing Infinitus agents into ChatGPT combines frontier AI with specialized healthcare capabilities while maintaining the safeguards healthcare demands. The plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation, including reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance. The new plugins join ChatGPT's broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research to documents, presentations, and software development.

OpenAI said healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, OpenAI is bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients. In a demo, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request, and the agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review. The articles give examples including a care coordinator using Luma Health to find tomorrow's appointments that still need confirmation and TriZetto to check insurance eligibility, and a primary care physician using Metriport to find a discharge summary and UpToDate to check follow-up monitoring. Other examples include an inpatient nurse using AIVA for a hospital's inpatient pump policy and Amion to find the covering endocrinologist, a care navigator using IMO Health, Stedi, and Turquoise Health to compare MRI sites, and a referral manager using Assort Health and Ferry Health for referral review.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, subject to workspace settings, and workspace administrators can enable new healthcare plugins. Individual clinicians have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, and select plugins are also available. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation, and both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows. Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, and customers can purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer by contacting the sales team. OpenAI said it is continuing to invest in the plugin ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with it.

stories.Headline: Moody's chief economist Mark Zandi warns AI boom raises inflation and borrowing costs while diverting investment
stories.Summary:
Moody's Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi warned on Sunday in a post on X that the artificial intelligence boom is driving up inflation and borrowing costs while pulling investment away from the rest of the U.S. economy. Zandi wrote that AI has been a boon to economic growth and job creation, but he said its rapid expansion is bringing significant economic side effects. He said AI is adding to inflation by driving up electricity and consumer electronics prices, and he said AI investment is pushing up interest rates by soaking up capital to finance the AI build-out. He cautioned that the massive flow of money into AI infrastructure is coming at the expense of other investment. Zandi said that since ChatGPT debuted four years ago, AI has gone from a rounding error to accounting for nearly two-thirds of the growth in investment.

He added that growth in everything else has slowed by more than half since mid-2024. He concluded with a warning about the economic returns expected from the technology, saying the bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity because the rest of the economy is not investing enough to deliver it. In September, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said AI infrastructure spending could reach $1 trillion in 2027, adding about 1% to GDP growth annually while potentially contributing to inflation, and he cautioned that it was too early to identify winners and losers in the AI boom. In July, the International Monetary Fund warned that weaker-than-expected AI productivity gains could trigger a pullback in technology investment and a sharp correction in highly valued tech stocks, while raising its 2026 global inflation forecast to 4.7%. Last month, economist Peter Schiff warned that rising borrowing costs could weaken AI investment and expose broader economic vulnerabilities, while potentially benefiting gold and gold-mining stocks during an impending recession.

Former Federal Reserve adviser Danielle DiMartino Booth also suggested a recession may already be underway. stories.Headline: Hitachi validates agentic AI platform that cuts chiplet design candidates by over 90%
stories.Summary:
Hitachi's Research and Development Group announced on November 12, 2026, that it had completed and empirically validated a foundational design platform for semiconductor chiplet package design. The platform combines autonomous agentic AI with ultra-fast surrogate physics models to streamline advanced semiconductor packaging. The announcement followed preliminary technical disclosures presented by Hitachi researchers at the 35th IEEE Conference on Electrical Performance of Electronic Packaging and Systems, known as EPEPS 2026. That conference was held in Fort Worth, Texas, from October 18 to 21, 2026. In verification trials using a heterogeneous package with three distinct chiplet types, Hitachi demonstrated that its agentic AI pruned the candidate design space by more than 90%.

Engineers provide high-level targets, thermal design power limits, footprint boundaries and cost goals in natural language, and the agentic AI structures these prompts into formal design-for-manufacturing rules. The system integrates procurement constraints, bill-of-materials availability and vendor lead times to discard unviable component pairings early. The engine concurrently evaluates candidate layouts across electrical performance, thermal dynamics and mechanical stress using accelerated AI surrogate models. Electrical performance covers signal latency, return loss and power impedance, thermal dynamics covers hotspot dissipation and junction temperatures, and mechanical stress covers warpage and shear strain from thermal expansion coefficient mismatches. Hitachi also announced on the same day a technology that uses quantum-inspired CMOS annealing to create a supply-demand plan covering more than 500 generators up to 36 hours ahead in 60 minutes.

Hitachi's Research and Development Group is responsible for the platform, and the company positions it as a foundational technology within its Lumada 3.0 digital transformation framework under its One Hitachi initiative. Hitachi aims to provide edge AI semiconductor engineering services across mobility, energy and robotics. Hitachi plans to conduct Proof-of-Concept engagements with commercial chip vendors, fabless design firms and packaging OSAT providers through late 2026 and 2027. Research teams are also extending surrogate models to support higher die counts, emerging optical interconnects and standard specifications from the UCIe consortium. Both the chiplet technology and the annealing technology remain at the verification stage, and the company is moving toward practical application.

Writing for Mynavi TECH+ on November 13, 2026, technology writer Yukio Kobayashi emphasized that component volatility remains a critical obstacle in chiplet projects. Kobayashi noted that incorporating procurement availability into early automated screening directly targets a common source of project delays. Writing for EE Times Japan on November 16, 2026, semiconductor journalist Takatsuna Mamoto underscored the value of concurrent tri-physics analysis. Mamoto observed that optimizing trace latency often concentrates heat dissipation, generating coefficient-of-thermal-expansion mismatches that can crack solder microbumps. Japanese industry portal Dellows News noted on November 13, 2026, that the technology arrives as edge AI and automotive electronics shift rapidly toward modular silicon, and that for mid-sized semiconductor firms lacking large dedicated packaging teams, automated exploration tools help bridge substantial resource gaps.

Advanced semiconductor packaging has become the primary mechanism for computational scaling as monolithic silicon approaches photolithographic reticle limits and rising wafer defect costs. Disaggregating system-on-chip architectures into modular chiplets such as compute cores, high-bandwidth memory and analog I/O controllers enables process-node optimization for each die. Assembling multiple dies onto high-density substrates creates an explosive combinatorial search space in which engineers must evaluate thousands of spatial floorplans, inter-die bump patterns, routing layers and stackups. With leading-edge fabrication costs climbing at sub-3nm nodes, monolithic dies larger than 800 square millimeters face severe yield penalties. Industry consortia and commercial leaders including the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express group have prioritized modular advanced packaging, while established commercial electronic design automation suites provide high accuracy for signoff verification but require hours or days of cluster compute time to evaluate a single package geometry.

Following validation on three-chiplet architectures, Hitachi is preparing broader industry rollouts. The articles leave open the results of the planned Proof-of-Concept engagements with commercial chip vendors, fabless design firms and packaging OSAT providers. The articles do not state when the platform will move beyond the verification stage to practical application. The articles do not give the outcome of efforts to extend surrogate models to higher die counts, emerging optical interconnects and UCIe standard specifications. The articles do not state the cost of the platform or when it will be commercially available.

stories.Headline: OpenAI releases a free image classifier that detects child sexual abuse material and flags AI-generated CSAM
stories.Summary:
OpenAI released a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material on November 16, 2026, according to its blog post. The tool is an image classifier that looks for visual signs of abuse in images. It returns scores that help reviewers decide which images may need attention first. OpenAI said this is the first broadly available CSAM classifier with a specific signal indicating if CSAM may be AI generated. OpenAI also released product warnings in ChatGPT, practical resources for developers, and support for child-safety law enforcement investigators.

The classifier is offered at no cost through the OpenAI API to vetted organizations, including child safety organizations and the broader industry. OpenAI trained and designed it with assistance from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, a nonprofit that operates the CyberTipline. In an evaluation of user-uploaded images, OpenAI estimated the new classifier would flag 48% fewer images while finding roughly the same number of abusive images as the existing tool. Images flagged by the new classifier were about twice as likely to contain abuse. In fal's testing on human-reviewed production images, reviewers confirmed 72% of the classifier's high-confidence flags as novel CSAM, invideo AI's testing showed one in four flagged cases led to a ban, and SafetyKit's evaluations involving drawings or animations that sexualize children found the classifier detected 90% of cases.

OpenAI said individual companies have a responsibility to prevent their technology from being exploited by predators to harm children. John Shehan, Senior Vice President at NCMEC, said technology has an essential role in helping identify CSAM and the children depicted in it. Shehan said the new classifier gives more organizations access to tools that can help detect previously unidentified CSAM and strengthen reporting. Thorn said protecting children requires more than any single solution or organization and commended OpenAI for working with organizations throughout the child protection ecosystem. OpenAI said it engaged the Tech Coalition and ROOST to help share access to the tool and recently began participating in the Tech Coalition's Lantern program.

A Childlight analysis at the University of Edinburgh found AI-related reports of CSAM increased globally by more than 8,400 percent from 2023 to 2025. Last year NCMEC received more than 400,000 of these reports, compared with roughly 4,700 in 2023. The ChatGPT warning makes clear that sexualizing children causes harm, including when the requested material is AI-generated. Alongside the warning, OpenAI will remove the flagged conversation and pause access to ChatGPT for 24 hours, while keeping specialist support available. Repeated violations may lead to longer restrictions and ultimately account closure or reports to authorities.

OpenAI developed the warning approach with input from Protect Children, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, Dr. Caoilte Ó Ciardha of the University of Kent, and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages. OpenAI published CSAM guidance developed with input from the Tech Coalition, Thorn, NCMEC, and the Internet Watch Foundation. OpenAI worked with Anthropic and Google to jointly commission guidance on responding to disclosures of child sexual exploitation and abuse in AI systems, recently published by the Tech Coalition. OpenAI said this guidance has led to increased numbers of developers accessing child safety tooling and registering to report CSAM to NCMEC. OpenAI said it already prohibits CSAM, trains its models to refuse requests for it, and takes action against accounts that violate its policies.

The first law enforcement tool will help investigators review lengthy chat logs and legal process returns, identify potential connections, and create timelines, with findings linked to source material. The initial training is planned as an overview and demonstration, supported by a practical field guide that teams can refer to afterward. Access will depend on agency authorization and program requirements. Future iterations of the training will be proposed at regional, national and international conferences. Organizations interested in the classifier will be able to request access through OpenAI's intake form, and OpenAI said it will continue improving the classifier with feedback from those that use it.

stories.Headline: Claroc finds Grok Build exposes corporate data for thousands of users
stories.Summary:
Security firm Claroc discovered that Grok Build exposed sensitive corporate data through weak default security designs and poor data management. This vulnerability affected thousands of users including Fortune 500 companies and defense contractors. The breach occurred because the platform used randomized URLs that were easily collected by passive DNS services. SpaceXSI, the new name for xAI, operated the Grok Build agent that caused these leaks. The findings were reported by the technology publication Ars Technica on November 16, 2026.

The system used subdomains ending in grok.me, such as failing-chassis-traders, which granted access without a separate login. Claroc found 37,571 online subdomains, and 35,578 of these exposed data because the default setting was Anyone with the link. Exposed data included 24 SpaceXSI apps with a sales map of 594 companies and a confidential onboarding plan. A Peruvian construction company had medical records for 3,784 workers exposed, and Tesla leaked data on 22 mechanics. Other leaks included U.S. Navy contractor rosters, a U.S. IT services hardware bill of materials, and Norwegian-Finnish aerospace explosives dashboards.

Claroc notified SpaceX of these security gaps on November 8 but received no response from the company. Ars Technica reported that SpaceXSI removed links to 24 internal applications within hours of an email inquiry. Claroc stated that no separate access restrictions were implemented for applications created by other users of the platform. The security firm explained that hostnames in the URL structure allowed outsiders to discover applications in large numbers. They noted that the default sharing permission for published applications remained open unless users manually changed the settings.

Other vibe coding platforms like Lovable, Bolt, and Replit may also allow addresses to be discovered through passive DNS. Moltbook exposed 1.5 million authentication tokens and 35,000 email addresses by embedding a Supabase API key in JavaScript. Cal AI leaked 14.59GB of data, totaling 3.2 million user records, due to an unauthenticated Google Firebase backend. Red Access found 5,000 assets from Lovable, Base44, Replit, and Netlify that exposed medical, financial, and corporate strategy documents. Meta Muse also had 6,800 shared links exposed through passive DNS records before suspending the feature on October 20.

Vibe coding allows non-developers to generate business software using natural language, voice, or text prompts. This trend prioritizes speed and easy deployment over security safeguards, leading to public-by-default settings and weak access controls. Many users add customer information and internal documents to these apps without conducting any formal security reviews. A June report by the Cloud Security Alliance titled The Vibe Coding Governance Gap highlighted these systemic issues. The articles state that security is often treated as an optional feature rather than a fundamental requirement.

Platforms should make private access the default and improve URL structures to prevent discovery by passive DNS services. Companies must identify AI-created applications and require security reviews for those handling internal documents or customer information. Authentication mechanisms must stop relying solely on obscuring URLs to protect sensitive corporate and personal data. The articles leave open whether SpaceXSI will implement broader access restrictions for all third-party users of Grok Build. It remains unclear if other platforms mentioned by Claroc have already fixed their passive DNS vulnerabilities.

stories.Headline: Samsung and SK Hynix gain bargaining power as Nvidia faces leadership turmoil
stories.Summary:
Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang on November 9, 2026, causing the company's shares to fall by 4.3 percent. This leadership vacuum has shaken the AI semiconductor supply chain while creating new opportunities for South Korean memory suppliers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Anonymous employees launched a website called Stand With Jensen to petition for the return of the former chief executive officer. This petition gathered roughly 110,000 signatures, including 60,000 shareholders and 5,000 employees, to demand that Huang be reinstated and treated fairly. Silicon Valley figures like Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan also joined the signature drive to support the former leader.

The situation involves high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM, and requires a diversified customer base to increase the bargaining power of the memory suppliers. Samsung Electronics signed a priority HBM4 supply deal with AMD in March and partnered with Anthropic to manufacture its own AI chips. SK Hynix holds a near-monopoly on memory supply for Google's in-house Tensor Processing Unit chips, which Google has begun selling externally. Other companies deploying self-developed chips in data centers include Amazon with Trainium and Microsoft with the Maia 100 chip. US lawmakers are now pressing for tighter controls on AI chip exports to China following the allegations involving Jensen Huang.

Erwin Cummins, a senior research staff engineer at Nvidia, stated that Huang's leadership was the driving force that brought employees to the company. Lee Ji-hwan, CEO of Aurora Investment Advisory, said memory demand is not significantly affected whether Nvidia wobbles or rivals like AMD and Google replace it. Kim Young-gun of Mirae Asset Securities diagnosed that Samsung and SK Hynix can strengthen bargaining power through the diversification of their customers. Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker said on X that facts must be verified and an investigation must determine if Huang serves shareholders. These experts believe that the shift from AI training to the inference phase will continue to underpin the demand for memory.

Dylan Patel, CEO of SemiAnalysis, said that Google and others might take significant market share because Huang is the only executive who can secure production. Major customers of Nvidia are reducing their dependence by developing application-specific integrated circuits, which is a trend that benefits the memory industry. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are affected by these shifts, as well as by the potential for tighter US export curbs to China. A fake letter impersonating Vice President Ian Buck and Chief Scientist Bill Dally circulated on X, demanding the resignation of the entire board. This fraudulent document was a modified version of the open letter from when OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was ousted in 2023.

The background shows that SK Hynix had about a quarter of its revenue coming from Nvidia during the previous year of business operations. The memory industry views the current reshuffle as an opportunity because more diversified chip design companies create a more stable demand base. The rise of competitors like AMD and Google is reshaping the supply chain as they target gaps in the market built by Nvidia. AI infrastructure investment is not expected to shrink, but the center of gravity is moving from the training phase to the inference phase. The trend of rising HBM content in advanced application-specific integrated circuits provides a tailwind for the South Korean memory companies.

Next, investors must watch trading volume and foreign flows to see if Samsung Electronics can enter a full-fledged uptrend in its share price. Market observers believe that the negotiating power of memory companies will rise further if the structure of diversified chip design takes hold. The industry must determine if the market can absorb the selling volume from investors who bought Samsung shares at past high prices. The articles leave open whether the independent investigation into Jensen Huang will result in his permanent removal or his eventual reinstatement. It remains uncertain how the push for tighter China chip curbs will specifically impact the future revenues of Samsung and SK Hynix.

stories.Headline: Bogdan Pătrăucean releases Wintoys 3.0 with an option to disable Windows 11 AI services
stories.Summary:
Wintoys 3.0, build 3.0.10.0, was released by developer Bogdan Pătrăucean and announced on Reddit, adding an AI components option under the Optimizations tab. The free tool is distributed through the Microsoft Store and runs on Windows 10 and Windows 11 through a WinUI 3 interface. The option disables background services such as WorkloadsSessionHost.exe, which hold machine-learning models in memory for features like Windows Recall and semantic search. Pătrăucean said those services can use 2GB to more than 8GB of RAM, including while the related features sit idle. On his 16GB Surface Pro 12, he reported that switching them off cut memory use from 11GB to about 5GB.

The option is limited to Copilot+ PCs with a neural processing unit, and on conventional desktops the entry is not expected to appear at all. Wintoys 3.0 also adds a separate Artificial Intelligence section for managing Recall, Click to Do, Notepad's writing tools and agentic search, with toggles depending on installed hardware and Windows features. Profiles exports and restores a Windows setup as a JSON file and requires the paid Wintoys+ add-on, a one-time purchase with lifetime access, while earlier functions remain free. A new Configuration mode applies settings as preferences or policies where the operating system supports it, improving synchronization with the Windows Group Policy Editor. The build also brings extra privacy controls, File Explorer preloading options, a reworked storage cleaner, clearer restart prompts and bug fixes.

Pătrăucean described the memory figures as individual observations rather than controlled benchmarks, and said actual savings will vary with hardware, software configuration and which AI workloads are active. He pointed to a Microsoft Q&A thread from July 2026 in which a different user described recovering about 5GB by halting the Windows AI Fabric service and its associated workload processes. He said the AI components option targets WorkloadsSessionHost.exe, which can run in multiple instances to keep models ready. He pitched Profiles at people setting up a fresh install or provisioning several machines. He said Configuration mode matters because policy refreshes can otherwise revert changes made by third-party tweakers.

The articles say disabling AI services can break the features that depend on them, and that users on work or organization-managed computers are advised to weigh the implications of each tweak because some changes may conflict with corporate configuration. The articles say Copilot+ machines ship with the AI stack enabled by default, and on 16GB configurations the resident models can consume a meaningful share of system memory. The articles say IT administrators may find the Group Policy synchronization the more consequential addition, since managed machines often have settings locked down by policy. The articles say the tool comes from an unverified third-party source rather than Microsoft's own settings app. The articles say Wintoys has been free since its launch and Profiles marks one of the first capabilities reserved for paying supporters.

The articles say Microsoft has worked to trim Windows 11's memory footprint, an effort the company has discussed publicly in recent months. The articles say Wintoys takes a more granular route by exposing individual components rather than waiting for Microsoft to retune them. The articles say the release lands as that Microsoft effort continues. The articles say Wintoys lets users manage system settings, uninstall applications, optimize performance and control privacy features. The articles say the update was detailed by the developer.

The articles say Wintoys 3.0 can be downloaded at no charge from the Microsoft Store. The articles say whether users who came for the memory savings will follow into the paid tier is an open question. The articles leave open the actual savings on other machines, since the figures are individual observations rather than controlled benchmarks. The articles leave open which toggles appear, since that depends on installed hardware and Windows features present on the system. The articles say users should review the implications of individual tweaks before applying them.

stories.Headline: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook forms emergency team to prevent AI cheating on 2027 CSAT
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced the creation of a pangovernment emergency response team on Monday, November 16, 2026. This action follows a YouTube confession on Sunday by the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam, who admitted to using generative AI and electronic devices to cheat. The government intends to use this team to prevent similar AI-assisted cheating during the 2027 academic year College Scholastic Ability Test, which takes place this Thursday.

The initiative requires the Ministry of Education to review how testing sites are proctored and managed to block sophisticated tools like smart glasses and ultrasmall electronic devices. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin visited Yeongdeungpo Girls’ High School on Monday to check safety and cheating preparations. Additionally, the Ministry of Education previously conducted safety inspections at 1,312 testing sites across 85 districts starting on October 20. The Human Resources Development of Korea also plans to file a criminal complaint against the tax accountant who cheated.

Prime Minister Han stated that cheating by a few must not erode confidence in the exam system or harm students who worked hard. She emphasized that existing management methods are too limited to handle varied AI techniques and called for thorough investigations if irregularities appear in results. Education Minister Choi promised a zero-tolerance principle toward cheaters and vowed to spare no effort to ensure a fair environment. He also briefed the National Assembly’s Education Committee on Monday regarding specific measures to block smart glasses.

The government is now focusing all national capabilities on the upcoming entrance exam to ensure that advanced AI is not exploited. Authorities will also investigate potential AI-assisted cheating across 528 different national exams to address the fundamental problem of exam integrity. Following the CSAT, the government plans to maintain strict oversight and use objective data to investigate any suspicious results. Relevant ministries have been told to promptly prepare similar preventive measures for all other exams under their jurisdiction.

stories.Summary:
US officials launched a fresh regulatory probe into Alibaba Group Holding regarding its cloud AI chip access. This investigation began around November 15, 2026, following allegations involving Nvidia's CEO and Alibaba cloud partners. Regulators are reviewing claims that Alibaba linked data centers to restricted Nvidia AI chips. The probe examines if remote access allowed Chinese clients to use processors subject to export controls. Officials want to know if this bypassed direct chip shipments to restricted users.

The probe focuses on Alibaba Cloud and its relationships with Nvidia and various cloud partners. It examines whether remote access to restricted Nvidia hardware violated US export rules in China. The company has a three year AI and cloud capex plan totaling RMB 380b. T Head has shipped 470,000 AI chips as part of this broader technology strategy. Alibaba also targets an ARR of RMB 16b plus for model and application services during 2026.

US regulators are responsible for the probe and are reviewing claims about restricted chip access. They are examining if cloud based access allowed Chinese clients to use restricted AI processors. The officials are investigating whether these actions bypassed the existing US export controls on hardware. Regulators are looking into the specific relationships between Alibaba cloud partners and the CEO of Nvidia. They are assessing if these links facilitated the unauthorized use of advanced AI technology.

Business customers using Alibaba cloud infrastructure are affected because the probe touches a core service. These merchants and enterprises rely on the technology capabilities linked to the broader retail platform. If regulators close off remote access, Alibaba may need to rework how AI workloads are provisioned. The company might have to adjust which customers it serves from specific data centers. This could lead to higher costs or lower performance for some of its services.

Alibaba runs a large commerce ecosystem and provides cloud infrastructure for enterprises in China and abroad. The company uses T Head for chip shipments and maintains a large AI spending narrative. This narrative relies on turning massive capex into profitable model and cloud services for its users. The business currently faces AI lab losses and negative free cash flow in its financial reports. Analysts have suggested a fair value of 186 for the company based on these catalysts.

stories.Headline: Altimeter Capital aims to invest $5 billion in the Anthropic IPO
stories.Summary:
Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Altimeter Capital aims to invest $5 billion in the Anthropic IPO. This planned investment is five times the largest amount Gerstner has ever put into an initial public offering. Anthropic is expected to go public on the Nasdaq this coming Thursday. This event marks a milestone as the first major AI lab to go public. It beats OpenAI, which is targeting its own IPO next year.

Anthropic plans to offer 825 million shares at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion. The current expected IPO price is between $70 and $78 a share. Leading chipmakers and cloud providers are collectively investing $26 billion at this price. These investors include Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Many of these firms are also customers of the AI company.

Brad Gerstner called the company a cornerstone compounder for a long time and said the trade is going there. He stated that the company is in an excellent position on the financials. Gerstner said he has confidence in interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress. He also sent a letter to the board pushing for a full investigation into Jensen Huang's tenure. Gerstner noted that Huang had not discussed a comeback as CEO with him.

President Donald Trump said he would not mind if Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Trump also claimed that Alice Huang may not be a spy. Some allies of Huang have built a war room to get him back. Others, including Gary Black, say there is zero chance the board brings him back. These critics cite a violation of company policy regarding relationships with subordinates.

The IPO comes after a downturn in semiconductors and a massive anti-AI swing in Washington. It also follows the saga involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO, according to a person familiar with the matter. The board is instead focused on a national security investigation into Huang. Last year, more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue was driven by China.

Anthropic will hit the market during this particularly tough moment for the industry. The articles leave open whether the board will ever change its mind about Jensen Huang. stories.Headline: Japanese manufacturers report higher profits as AI demand lifts earnings

These financial gains occurred during the period from April to September and were driven by the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Firms within the manufacturing sector performed particularly well as they capitalized on the robust demand for new technology. Several of these organizations have already revised their full-year earnings forecasts upward to reflect this growth. The current economic shift requires these companies to adapt their production and financial planning to meet the surging demand for AI.

This trend changes the outlook for the manufacturing sector by increasing the expected revenue for the remainder of the fiscal year. Every firm that closes its books in March must now account for these unexpected gains in their official reports. The surge in profits indicates a broader transition toward integrating artificial intelligence across various industrial applications. Yoshimitsu Goto, who serves as the Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of SoftBank Group, spoke about these developments.

He addressed the current business climate during an online news conference held on Tuesday to discuss the financial landscape. While the specific details of his remarks were not fully detailed, his presence highlighted the importance of the AI boom. He represents a major player in the technology sector that is closely monitoring these market shifts. The broader context involves a period of significant growth for Japanese firms despite growing uncertainty in the global market.

These companies are leveraging the AI boom to strengthen their positions against international competitors in the tech space. stories.Headline: Sharjah Digital Department launches Agentic AI Challenge to automate government operations
stories.Summary:
The Sharjah Digital Department launched the Sharjah Agentic AI Challenge to speed up the use of agentic artificial intelligence in government operations. This initiative follows the directives of HH Sheikh Sultan bin Mohammed bin Sultan Al Qasimi, the Crown Prince and Deputy Ruler of Sharjah. The event is scheduled to take place from December 8 to 10 to help automate various government services and operations. It is organized in partnership with Inception42, while Microsoft is participating as a collaborator for the duration of the challenge. The program aims to empower national talent to create innovative solutions that address real world challenges using new agentic AI technologies.

The challenge is open to the public and will include 30 participants who will work in teams of specialists and experts. These teams must develop prototypes of intelligent AI agents that can automate repetitive procedures and reduce the time for processing transactions. The program uses a design thinking approach and hands on learning under the guidance of trainers to create these practical solutions. It begins with an introductory session and three days of intensive work from 8 to 10 December in the city. The final prototypes will be presented to a specialized judging panel that will select the winning teams for the competition.

Sheikh Saud bin Sultan Al Qasimi, Director General of Sharjah Digital Department, said the Crown Prince set a clear strategic objective for them. He stated that the goal is to harness the potential of agentic AI in practical ways across various government institutions. He believes the true value of these technologies is their ability to streamline procedures and improve the quality of government services. He noted that the challenge is a practical step toward building sustainable government capabilities by combining operational experience with technical knowledge. He added that this will strengthen institutional integration and support the goals of the Sharjah Digital Transformation Strategy 2026 to 2028.

The project is designed to make a tangible difference to the lives of people by improving the overall customer experience. It affects national talent by providing them with the opportunity to develop solutions that enhance the efficiency of government operations. The initiative also aims to strengthen partnerships and integration between different entities to promote a sustainable digital transformation for the region. These efforts align with the human centred approach to digital integration that Sharjah has committed to for its citizens and residents. The challenge also supports the broader goals of the We the UAE 2031 Vision and the UAE National Strategy for AI.

The Sharjah Digital Transformation Strategy 2026 to 2028 aims to develop government services and improve the performance of various local institutions. This strategy provides the background for the current challenge to promote a sustainable digital transformation across the entire government sector. The UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 also serves as a foundation for these technological advancements in the emirate. Additionally, the We the UAE 2031 Vision guides the strategic direction for integrating advanced technology into the national infrastructure and services. These frameworks emphasize the importance of strengthening digital capabilities to maintain a competitive and efficient government for the future.

The next step involves the introductory session followed by three days of intensive practical work for the thirty selected challenge participants. Teams will collaborate to turn specific challenges into practical solutions before presenting their final prototypes to the specialized judging panel. The panel will then evaluate the work to select the winning teams based on the quality of their AI agents. The articles do not state what rewards the winning teams will receive after the competition ends on December 10. They also leave open how the winning prototypes will be implemented into actual government operations after the challenge is completed.

stories.Headline: Air Marshal Tejinder Singh highlights AI's role in future military capabilities at Pune seminar
stories.Summary:
Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, spoke about the strategic importance of Artificial Intelligence in shaping future military capabilities and operational preparedness, according to a Defence Ministry official. He made his remarks at a seminar held as part of a three-day Capsule on Science, Technology and Applied Research Programme at the Military Institute of Technology in Pune. The seminar carried the theme of AI versus AI as a new frontier of warfare and brought together tri-service leadership along with technology experts from academia and industry. Those present deliberated on the changing character of warfare in the AI era, the Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said in a post on the social media platform X. The seminar included sessions by subject matter experts from the Armed Forces, academia and industry that covered emerging AI technologies, Sovereign AI, AI-enabled weapon systems, autonomous and counter-autonomous systems, human-machine teaming and decision superiority in multi-domain operations.

A key highlight was an event called Navonmesh, described as a meeting place for innovation and new ideas, where leading industry partners showcased cutting-edge AI technologies and innovative solutions along with their potential military applications. The seminar reinforced the importance of jointness, indigenous technological capabilities and collaboration between the Armed Forces, academia and industry in preparing for the evolving challenges of future warfare. Before the seminar, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh visited the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla in Pune, where he reviewed key training infrastructure, the curriculum and forthcoming development projects aimed at further enhancing the training environment. The Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said he also visited the outdoor tactical training site and interacted with cadets undergoing camp training, gaining insights into their training experiences and professional development. Addressing the cadets, he urged them to uphold the highest traditions of military ethos and to imbibe the core values of discipline, integrity and dedication while fostering a spirit of jointness.

He further urged them to strive for professional excellence and to prepare themselves to shoulder future responsibilities, carrying forward the legacy of what the statement called a distinguished cradle of military leadership. In a separate message, the Indian Air Force said on X that a exercise named AJHE26 was set to commence at Air Force Station Jamnagar from November 17 to 19, 2026. That exercise will bring together the Indian Defence Forces, the National Disaster Management Authority, the Indian Coast Guard and friendly foreign countries, according to the Indian Air Force message. The stated aim of the exercise is to strengthen joint preparedness and coordination in disaster response among the participating forces and agencies. The articles do not say what decisions, if any, followed from the seminar or the academy visit, and they give no further details on the outcomes of either.

stories.Headline: Young South Koreans use AI to create fake funeral portraits as a prank
stories.Summary:
Young South Koreans are using generative artificial intelligence to create fake funeral portraits of themselves or their friends as a joke. This social media trend was reported on November 15, 2026, as a growing practice among the youth in Seoul. The prank involves posting these AI images on Instagram accompanied by memorial messages to trick people into thinking they died. Many of these posts are designed to look like genuine death announcements to confuse the people who see them. This trend has prompted various news reports to call for tighter regulation of the online platforms where they appear.

The posts feature black and white images styled as funeral portraits with phrases like Rest in peace or You will always be remembered. Some images include fabricated dates of death and dates of birth, along with white chrysanthemums and black ribbons for added realism. This specific practice has recently gained popularity among teenagers and people in their 20s as a prank among close friends. The images are shared on Instagram, which is the primary platform where this surge of AI generated content is occurring. These visual elements make the fake portraits very difficult to distinguish from real announcements of a person's passing.

Kim Si-deok is a professor in the department of funeral services at Eulji University who spoke to the South Korean media. He stated that younger generations are increasingly taking the significance of death and funeral traditions lightly through this specific social trend. The professor warned that this behavior trivialises death and urged online platforms to take steps to prevent such content from spreading. Meta, the parent company of Instagram, responded by saying it removes or restricts content that violates its community standards. The company told a local news outlet that it will continue working with outside organisations to maintain a safe environment.

Some people who are aware of the prank ask what food they should prepare for the fake memorial service in comments. Others are unaware that the posts are fake and offer sincere condolences, saying it is heartbreaking to see someone die young. Experts are affected by this trend and have called for stronger action from social media platforms to stop the practice. Meta noted that users can report manipulated images of private individuals, including minors, that are shared without their own consent. The company claims it promptly removes such content following a review to protect the users on its social platform.

The articles provide background on how generative AI is being used to create these deceptive images for social media entertainment. This trend is part of a broader context of AI use in South Korea, including fake chats and exam cheating. One mentioned case involved a man making over 100 prank calls to police to be sent to a jail. Another instance involved an actor named Lee Yi kyung whose lewd chats were created by an accuser using AI tools. These examples show a pattern of using artificial intelligence for deception or pranks within the South Korean society.

Meta will continue to review and remove manipulated images of private individuals that are reported by users on the Instagram platform. The company intends to keep working with relevant outside organisations to ensure that the social media environment remains safe. The articles leave open whether the calls for tighter regulation of online platforms will lead to new laws or rules. It is unclear if the trend among teenagers and people in their 20s will decrease after these expert warnings. The reports do not state if any specific legal actions will be taken against those posting the fake portraits.

stories.Headline: Anthropic launches Nasdaq IPO to fund frontier models amid AI industry backlash
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is launching an initial public offering on the Nasdaq this Thursday, November 19, 2026, to raise money for its frontier models. The company is going public during a difficult period for the technology industry, which is currently facing a nationwide artificial intelligence backlash. This event follows a major political shift in Washington, D.C., and the sudden ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang early Thursday. The IPO arrives as investors seek a bright spot after the Nasdaq dropped 5.3 percent in October, its worst month since March 2025. This offering is considered a defining event for the young artificial intelligence market and the most important tech IPO in several years.

The IPO price is expected between 70 and 78 dollars a share, with a valuation of 1.4 trillion dollars and six times oversubscription. Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, and Advanced Micro Devices are collectively investing 26 billion dollars at this price. Anthropic has 900 billion dollars in spending commitments, including 110 billion dollars over ten years with Amazon and 400 billion dollars for cloud capacity. The lab committed 300 billion dollars to chip and data center partners and 125 billion to 150 billion dollars for Google chips. Google will own 13 percent of the company and backstop 19 billion dollars in lease commitments to Terawulf for Kentucky data centers.

Anthropic stated in its prospectus that it previously underestimated compute requirements, which constrained its capacity and impacted both product development and deployment. The company recorded a net loss of 104 billion dollars through the first nine months of 2026 before this public offering. Joe Fath of Eclipse called the staggering numbers hard to wrap one's head around, while David Tollen called it smart investing. Subhadeep Chatterjee, a former Google cloud partnerships leader, stated that everyone knows Anthropic is going to be the future of Google. Eli Mansoor of OskaQ Consulting said companies must rush to get infrastructure or they will be out of business.

The IPO affects major tech giants who need Anthropic's massive spending to continue for many years to come to drive the AI buildout. Corey Quinn of Duckbill said it is almost certain that the ten year Amazon contract will be renegotiated before it culminates. Investors are currently strained by rising interest rates, which have pushed them out of debt heavy neoclouds that are critical for infrastructure. Democratic victories in midterm elections and new ballot measures may potentially limit the development of new data centers across the country. Nvidia shareholders are affected as shares tumbled 13 percent this week to their lowest levels since July 2025 following the scandal.

Anthropic is a five year old company that has never lived through a technology downturn but is now burning historic amounts of money. The company has 132 billion dollars in existing cash and short term investments and could yield over 90 billion dollars in proceeds. Amazon previously built a custom chip data center in Indiana specifically for Anthropic, while cloud partners account for 31 percent of obligations. Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley offered 63 billion dollars to buy Broadcom AI chip racks for Anthropic to rent. Broadcom has provided a backstop for these rentals with a maximum liability of 43 billion dollars to support the lab.

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Cress faces a major test on Tuesday when the company reports quarterly results two days before the Anthropic debut. A data center for Anthropic that starts leasing in 2027 has a unique twenty year term to ensure future computing capacity. The articles leave open whether the explosive growth of the company can outpace its massive expenses as Jim Cramer questioned. It remains uncertain if the AI trade will be revived or if Nvidia's competitors will capture a greater share of the market. The market is still tracking three scenarios to determine how the artificial intelligence trade will be resolved in the coming months.

stories.Headline: Huawei Horinger data center has 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX Colossus 2
stories.Summary:
Ben Cottier and Lynette Bye of Epoch AI analyzed Huawei's Horinger data center on November 12, 2026. They found the facility has roughly 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX's Colossus 2. The researchers used satellite imagery and public sources to reach this specific conclusion. They noted that Huawei is using China's abundant energy to build these large centers. The analysis suggests the facility will stay far behind Colossus 2 until at least 2028.

The Horinger campus in Inner Mongolia has three zones called West, South, and North. It has up to 286 megawatts of IT power capacity across four buildings. These buildings use Ascend 910C and 910B chips, totaling 105,000 and 8,000 units respectively. Colossus 2 is located in Tennessee and is the largest AI data center globally. The Horinger site is compared to the 1.8 million H100-equivalents expected for Colossus 2.

Epoch AI researchers estimated the compute by modeling the heat rejection of rooftop cooling equipment. They stated that the Horinger facility is likely one of the largest in China. The authors noted that US facilities extract 2.5 times more compute per unit of power. They explained that the 910C chip performs at around 0.76 of an H100 equivalent. They concluded that China's compute constraints are unlikely to ease in the next two years.

The report mentions that VNET Bayin Ulanqab and Huawei Wuhu might match Horinger's capacity. Users of these systems are affected by the gap in chip performance and efficiency. A commenter named Mira noted that cooling towers provide a physical audit of compute. Another person named Sam Quiring questioned if banned Nvidia chips were used at the site. These individuals highlighted the importance of performance per watt over simple megawatt capacity.

Huawei is China's biggest AI chip developer but faces strict US export controls on technology. The Horinger campus was built after villages were demolished to make way for the centers. The facility uses hypernode servers designed for large-model training and inference for various end users. Most of the chips used were sold by the end of March 2026. The researchers observed moving cooling fans and water vapor to confirm the buildings operate.

One building in the West zone should become operational by December 2026 to increase capacity. Three new buildings are planned, with one in the South zone expected by February 2028. This growth could increase the total AI compute of the campus by over 70 percent. The articles leave open whether the overall frontier of Chinese data centers will fall further. They do not state if other Chinese facilities will close the gap with the US.

stories.Headline: Dublin City Council pilots AI flood warning system with EMR Integrated Solutions
stories.Summary:
Dublin City Council will pilot a new artificial intelligence early warning system for major flood events in Dublin City, the Irish Examiner reported on Monday, 16 November, 2026. The project is run in partnership with critical infrastructure specialist EMR Integrated Solutions, which gathered the sensor data used by the model. The pilot is set to run through this autumn and winter, according to the Irish Examiner. Silicon Republic reported that the rollout covers the autumn and winter of late 2026 and early 2027. Trials of the technology using historical events showed potential early warnings of 13 to 21 hours for some mountain rain-driven events.

The AI model draws on ten years' worth of sensor data gathered by EMR Integrated Solutions, including river level readings, rainfall measurements, tide data and data from Met Éireann. The project could warn between 13 and 21 hours ahead of events, which Dublin City Council says will give staff and response teams more time to prepare and act. EMR has operated Dublin City Council's regional flood monitoring system for nine years through outstations in the city and surrounding counties that monitor rainfall, river levels, tide readings and more. EMR was founded in the 1980s and is based in Dunboyne, Co Meath, and works with sectors including water, power, utilities, corporate business, broadcasting and public safety organisations. EMR has an agreement with Dublin City Council to provide engineers to support the council's flood management through associated site work, installations, repairs and instrument calibration.

Minister for Climate, Environment and Energy Darragh O'Brien, TD, welcomed the initiative and said the single most valuable thing we can give people is time. O'Brien said the pilot shows how AI can turn the data we already have into earlier, clearer warnings, helping engineers and emergency services make better decisions when it matters most. He said he very much welcomed the initiative from EMR Integrated Solutions and Dublin City Council and looked forward to seeing the results. Dublin City Council chief executive Richard Shakespeare said the pilot is likely to demonstrate how technology and data can be harnessed to support better decision-making and improve preparedness for flooding events. Shakespeare said the council is committed to further embracing appropriate AI technology that helps protect communities, homes and critical infrastructure as climate change increases the frequency and intensity of severe weather events.

EMR chief commercial officer Mark O'Connor said we know we can't stop the rain, nor can we prevent every flood, but we can potentially give people something they cannot buy, time to prepare and prevent, and time for the council to take action. Dennis Keeley, Dublin City Council's assistant chief executive for climate and urban resilience, said one of the greatest challenges during flooding events is ensuring operational teams have sufficient time to deploy resources, protect critical infrastructure and respond effectively to emerging risks. Keeley said the AI technology could help reduce disruption to communities, minimise damage to public assets and enhance public safety during extreme weather events. According to EMR, a central principle for the pilot system is that all decisions remain with qualified Dublin City Council staff, who can review and interpret alerts generated by the AI model based on its analysis of signals and patterns in the relevant data. EMR said the project aims to allow timely delivery of accurate and relevant information to residents who may be affected, supporting greater awareness, preparedness and community resilience.

Shakespeare said the pilot aligns strongly with the ambitions set out in the Dublin City Council Corporate Plan, particularly the commitment to building a climate-resilient city and delivering high-quality public services through innovation and collaboration. He referred to recent engagements with telemetry and SCADA provider EMR Integrated Solutions. O'Brien said we have seen in the past the devastating effect flooding has on homes, businesses and communities around Dublin. The Irish Examiner reported that trials of the tech show it can give between 13 and 21 hours of early warnings for some mountain rain-driven events. The AI model will rapidly analyse the data sets provided to staff and then give a more reliable warning of conditions which could lead to serious flooding.

The pilot is set to run through this autumn and winter, and Silicon Republic reported the rollout covers the autumn and winter of late 2026 and early 2027. O'Brien said he looked forward to seeing the results of the initiative from EMR Integrated Solutions and Dublin City Council. Shakespeare said the pilot is likely to demonstrate how technology and data can be harnessed to support better decision-making and improve preparedness for flooding events. According to EMR, all decisions remain with qualified Dublin City Council staff, who can review and interpret alerts generated by the AI model. The articles do not state what will happen after the pilot ends or whether the system will be made permanent.

stories.Headline: Apple adds macOS 27.3 beta warnings that limit app device control as AI apps grow
stories.Summary:
Apple introduced new security warnings in the macOS 27.3 beta to limit how apps control devices. These changes were released on Monday, November 16, 2026, to give Mac users more data control. The update specifically targets the access granted to apps that use AI agents for their workflows. Apple informed developers about these upcoming changes to the device control and data access APIs. This move comes as AI apps have grown in popularity among users of the operating system.

The update splits the Device Control and Data Access setting into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. Users will now select requesting apps from a list to grant permissions for specific folders or apps. A transparency indicator will appear in the Mac menu bar when an app controls another via the override. Users can also configure apps to ask for access each time instead of granting unrestricted device control. Entitlement details for developers are coming soon to help maintain experiences for new installations of the software.

Apple stated that these changes make it clearer to users what they are permitting when granting app access. The company said developers must adjust onboarding so apps can gracefully handle access to a limited set of folders. Apple noted that known apps will keep their current experience and existing permissions will remain in effect. The company wants to better inform users about the data apps receive when full permissions are granted. This effort aims to provide more granular control over the data shared with various third party applications.

Some users believe the move is good for raising awareness about the dangers of AI infiltrating a Mac. One user complained that the blue transparency indicator looks atrocious on the new PROLED MBP dynamic island. This person claimed that the new prompt replaces the old Accessibility Permissions and requires entering an admin password. Other users expressed frustration that they must download gigabytes of AI software even if they have no interest. These affected users must now navigate a settings page with red buttons to authorize their favorite third party apps.

Apple said last month that additional controls for Full Disk Access were necessary because of risks from AI agents. The company warned that some developers use Full Disk Access in ways that can put Mac users at risk. Such access can expose sensitive files, mail, messages, and browsing history to the application requesting the full control. These security concerns drove the decision to overhaul the APIs and introduce the new transparency indicator for users. The background of this change is rooted in the potential for AI agents to misuse broad system permissions.

Developers must now request entitlements to offer the same experience for new installations that existed before macOS 27.3. Mac users will encounter these new warnings and indicators when they approve new app permission requests on their devices. The articles leave open whether the entitlement process will work for apps that are not available in the store. It remains unclear if users can permanently acknowledge an app to remove the bright blue indicator from the island. The text does not specify when the final version of macOS 27.3 will be released to the public.

stories.Headline: ECB vice president Boris Vujčić warns rapid AI expansion threatens EU financial stability
stories.Summary:
European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujčić warned on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence could threaten financial stability in the region. Speaking at Euro Finance Week in Frankfurt, the official noted that stock market valuations for AI remain stretched and the risk of a repricing has risen. He observed that a recent correction following the mid-term elections in America serves as a necessary reminder for the industry to remain cautious. Vujčić argued that system-wide stability is now threatened by a range of additional factors beyond simple market valuations.

These risks include the expansion of external funding from equity to debt markets and the concentration of exposures across the sector. The Vice President also highlighted the dangers of quickening AI adoption and the potential for devastating cyberattacks against financial institutions. He emphasized that a resilient banking sector is critical given current geopolitical headwinds and elevated risks to overall stability. Furthermore, he stated that supervision must be maintained over non-banks, specifically mentioning the rapid growth of the private credit space.

Boris Vujčić explained that private credit warrants close monitoring because of limited transparency and growing interconnectedness with insurers and banks. He expressed concern regarding potential liquidity mismatches that could arise within these less transparent financial environments. These warnings follow a report from the International Monetary Fund titled Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity in the Financial Sector. The organization argued that AI can accelerate the discovery of vulnerabilities and turn isolated incidents into correlated disruptions affecting many institutions.

The report suggests that AI transforms cyber risk from a technical security concern into a broader issue of enterprise governance. It questions how much autonomy these systems should receive and whether organizations can contain them when something goes wrong. The International Monetary Fund noted that AI does not need to invent new forms of attack to change the risk equation. Instead, powerful models can cause significant damage when they are given network access or credentials in poorly configured environments.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Hackers steal Uber drivers license data via Fireworks AI credentials
stories.Summary:
Uber is notifying drivers that hackers stole personal information, including driver's license details, after attackers used stolen internal credentials at AI inference vendor Fireworks AI to reach Uber data. The breach notices were filed with state attorneys general and reported by TechCrunch on November 13. A third-party service provider notified Uber on October 9 that hackers had stolen its internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account with the provider. On October 13, Uber determined that the hackers had accessed its data, including personal information belonging to drivers. Uber confirmed to Gizmodo that the compromised provider was Fireworks AI, a startup that helps developers access and use open AI models.

State filings count at least 7,870 people in three states, a floor that will rise because Uber has not disclosed a national total. Massachusetts counted 2,567 people notified, South Carolina's Department of Consumer Affairs listed 3,430 affected residents, and Rhode Island counted 1,873. Illinois residents were also affected but that count was pending, and California drivers were notified without a published figure. A notice dated November 10 was filed with California's attorney general. Uber is offering affected drivers free credit monitoring and fraud assistance through Cyberscout, and drivers have 90 days from the date of their notification letter to sign up.

Fireworks told Uber on October 9 that hackers had broken in and stolen internal credentials, which the attackers then used to reach Uber's data. An Uber spokesperson tied the notices to a security incident at third-party vendor Fireworks.ai. Fireworks confirmed to TechCrunch that it identified unauthorized access affecting customer data but did not answer specific questions about the incident. Fireworks links the intrusion to a financially motivated criminal group that sells tokens obtained through unauthorized access to AI models, and no known group has claimed the theft of Uber's data. Uber said it immediately cut off its data connections with Fireworks after learning of the breach.

Fireworks says more than 10,000 companies use it, with Uber among its customers. Fireworks says it identified the activity at 12 p.m. ET on October 6, and that the attacker captured environment variables, including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, in evaluation jobs for a limited number of customer accounts. It says it began notifying affected customers on October 7, told identified affected customers at 9 p.m. ET on October 9, and published its public bulletin at 1 a.m.

ET on October 10. That bulletin said Fireworks had not detected evidence of unauthorized access to personal information within its security perimeter or control, based on its investigation at that time. Fireworks says it detected no impact to Inference, its Training SDK or Nexus, all of which run with zero data retention by default. On October 23, a third-party cloud provider that hosted Fireworks research-and-development machines had its own security incident, and on October 24 an unauthorized party used that access to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload. Fireworks says the exposed data included resource metadata, billing information such as addresses, invoice and payment history, account balances and credit usage, and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers, while payment card numbers were not stored and so were not affected.

As of October 25, it had found no further evidence of successful unauthorized access to the customer-facing platform, and it is working with Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42. Fireworks disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads for batch inference and dataset-based training while it investigates. Fireworks said it notified law enforcement and has been working with cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 to conduct forensic analysis. Fireworks told Notion on the evening of November 2 that a small dataset had been accessed by malicious actors, and Notion disconnected from Fireworks and deleted its data there the next morning. On November 6 Fireworks said potential customer data may have been accessed, and on November 8 it confirmed a new dataset.

That dataset included Notion AI chat transcripts from the Insights feature, tied to fewer than 1% of workspaces, and for most affected workspaces the transcripts cannot be tied to a user, workspace or company. Notion says this was not a breach of its own systems; it disabled Insights, stopped serving open-weight models through Fireworks, and told affected customers to rotate any credentials pasted into Notion AI. The Register, citing Bloomberg, reported that Fireworks is also working with customers including Cursor and Harvey to assess the impact. Uber's 2016 incident exposed names and license numbers of around 600,000 U.S. drivers, stored on a third-party cloud-based service.

State attorneys general alleged Uber failed to notify affected people promptly, and Uber agreed to a $148 million settlement with all 50 state attorneys general in 2018. The 2022 leak of employee data through the vendor Teqtivity, which affected more than 77,000 employees, was another vendor-origin incident. TechCrunch counts the current incident as Uber's second known breach this year, after an Uber Freight intrusion that an extortion gang claimed. In August, a hacking group claimed to have stolen nearly 1 million files from Uber Freight, the company's logistics subsidiary, and Uber Freight confirmed that attackers had gained unauthorized access.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong companies and family offices invest in AI financial analyst ARTi
stories.Summary:
An AI financial analyst named ARTi launched in July to provide investment research. Hong Kong listed companies and family offices made strategic investments in the startup. The product was incubated from a family office business system in Hong Kong. It allows users to inquire about stock trends and quotes via chat. The tool can also generate investment research reports for its users.

Delin Holdings, listed as 1709.HK, made a strategic investment in the platform. C Capital provided 1.5 million US dollars in Pre-A round funding in June. This investment gave the company a pre-money valuation of 30 million US dollars. The product reached 70,000 users within four months of its official launch. It connects to communication platforms like WhatsApp instead of requiring a new App.

CEO Eason Zhang said the tool solves the problem of information overload. He stated that every investment judgment made by the AI must be verifiable. Zhang believes professional agents need specific data sources and financial analysis frameworks. He noted that general large models often prefer guessing over admitting uncertainty. The team uses multi-model collaboration to establish a system for result verification.

High-net-worth investors and beginners, including Hong Kong university students, use the service. Some users from Delin's wealth management business provide core customer feedback. These professional investors require continuous tracking and clear frameworks for their research. Many users have expressed a willingness to pay for these professional services. The product currently serves as a value-added service for certain high-net-worth clients.

Eason Zhang previously served as a strategic consulting partner at a global firm. He founded a fintech enterprise after leaving that consulting role in 2015. The startup combines Silicon Valley AI technology with Hong Kong financial business resources. CTO Steve brings experience from Silicon Valley entrepreneurship to the technical architecture. A chief scientist from a Silicon Valley laboratory serves as an expert consultant.

The company has started its Series A financing to grow the business. ARTi plans to launch a subscription model with various monthly paid packages. These tiers are designed at 20, 100, and 200 US dollars per month. Paid users will gain access to virtual trading functions and research services. The articles leave open when large-scale charging will officially begin for users.
