Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin admitted that authorities cannot guarantee the detection of AI cheating before the college entrance exam. This admission occurred on November 16 during a National Assembly Education Committee meeting held in Yeouido, Seoul. The minister spoke during a plenary meeting while answering questions from lawmakers about the security of the upcoming test. He acknowledged that countermeasures against miniature cameras and similar equipment would probably not be perfect for the examination. These statements were made just two days before the start of the College Scholastic Ability Test in Korea.

The government will now require candidates to surrender smart devices and block public Wi-Fi at all examination centers. Authorities also announced the formation of an interagency task force to handle the threat of AI assisted cheating. These new measures were announced on November 16 to protect the integrity of the largest annual national examination. The government is also ordering a retrospective review of 528 national exams following a major AI cheating scandal. These changes aim to prevent the use of sophisticated electronic devices during the high stakes university admission process.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin told People Power Party Rep. Park Jeong-hun that he could not identify every cheating case. He stated that he did not think the government could guarantee the detection of all AI assisted cheating attempts. The prime minister demanded vigorous effort to prevent violations and called for harsh punishment for those who cheat. He emphasized that the nation must prepare carefully as it approaches the biggest test day of the year. The minister's candid remarks have led some to describe his current position as irresponsible given the timing.

Some students and parents are demanding that the CSAT be postponed because of the intense fear of cheating. These groups worry that the fairness of university admissions will be undermined if the government cannot stop AI. Other affected parties include candidates in professional qualification exams, university essay tests, and various school based academic assessments. The public confidence in the system that determines educational opportunities for young people is now at serious risk. Many feel that the government responses lag far behind the rapidly evolving methods used by those who cheat.

AI cheating became more apparent after the top scorer on the certified tax accountant examination made several shocking revelations. In May, a candidate in Gwangju was caught using AI equipped glasses during a fire protection engineering certification exam. Prosecutors sought a summary judgment against that candidate for violating the National Technical Qualifications Act during the May test. Other cases have emerged in the Law School Admission Test, English proficiency tests, and various national professional qualification examinations. Online vendors have openly sold cheating kits, and button camera sets have reportedly sold out to prospective examinees.

The government must now procure and install additional equipment, which presents considerable practical difficulties with only two days remaining. Authorities must decide if they can comprehensively restrict communication between the examination rooms and all outside parties. Other countries have already revised professional exams, prohibited digital devices, or introduced measures to block all wireless communications. The articles leave open whether the current interagency task force can actually ensure a fair testing environment for students. stories.Summary:
China plans to make artificial intelligence literacy universal for its nearly 200 million primary and secondary schoolchildren by 2030. The Ministry of Education has encouraged schools to develop pilot programs, train teachers, and launch specialized courses since 2024. This initiative ranges from teaching basic concepts in primary grades to utilizing complex tools and critical thinking for projects. The plan requires nearly half of all provinces and municipalities to implement mandatory AI plus education strategies.

Shanghai now requires at least 30 hours of AI skills training per year for every grade level. Beijing intends to establish 100 demonstration schools and use AI to monitor the health of students. The Ningxia and Gansu regions aim to include AI literacy in school entrance examinations by 2027, while Yunnan province plans to record and analyze lessons in 14,000 classrooms. Public procurement documents show that authorities have committed at least $31 million for learning platforms, teacher training, and classroom equipment.

The Ministry of Education is responsible for the broad push, while local leaders like Principal Yang Tianliang in Funan County, Anhui province, manage specific applications. Yang explained that AI agents ask students questions instead of providing immediate answers to help address a shortage of qualified teachers. At the Beijing New Talent Academy, thirteen-year-old student Peng Gaodi noted that he used AI to create over 200 applications, including a homework submission platform. The school in Anhui utilizes developments from Z.AI, ByteDance, and Alibaba's Qwen models.

China currently lacks a unified standard for assessing AI literacy, leaving individual schools to experiment with their own methods. One study of nearly 27,000 teenagers linked AI use to an 18 percent increase in homework grades but a 20 percent drop in monthly exam results. A separate survey of over 320,000 students highlighted risks of dependency and a decline in independent thinking. Students using AI at least three times weekly showed lower scores in creative, analytical, comprehension, and memory skills.

Test-takers must hand in all smart devices, and the government will scrutinize results for implausibly high scores after the exam. Confirmed cheaters face stern penalties, including the nullification of their results, restrictions on future exams, and criminal investigations. Additionally, the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the Human Resources Development Service of Korea will overhaul national certification exams by installing smart screening gates.

Prime Minister Han stated that fairness in exams is a basic principle that upholds trust in society and must not be damaged. She urged officials to mobilize every capability to create a fair environment while ensuring that honest students do not suffer. Han also ordered the immediate voiding of results for the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam who admitted to cheating. This individual will be barred from taking the exam for five years while the police conduct a rigorous investigation.

The government believes existing management is limited against new AI cheating techniques, leading to the creation of a pangovernment task force. This group will review how various ministries manage exams to establish common responses against smart device violations. Authorities will also operate a center for reporting cheating and investigate suspicious cases alongside the police. stories.Headline: Reporter uses AI glasses to solve difficult CSAT math questions in 22 minutes
stories.Summary:
A Kyunghyang Shinmun reporter used AI glasses to solve 2026 College Scholastic Ability Test questions on November 16. The reporter tested the device on math, Korean, and science sections to see if cheating was possible. The AI solved difficult math killer questions in one to two minutes and easier items in five seconds. All thirty math questions were finished in 22 minutes, resulting in a score of 98. The reporter also solved twenty science questions in 12 minutes and 44 seconds, scoring 34 out of 50.

The reporter used Rokid Glass AI from the Chinese company Rokid, which was released last January. These glasses cost about 750 dollars, weigh 49 grams, and look like ordinary horn-rimmed glasses with a small camera. The reporter used the Gemini AI model, which required a 20 minute setup before starting the test problems. The device allows users to choose specific AI models and perform training with detailed prompts for better accuracy. The reporter touched the temple of the glasses to trigger the camera and display answers on the lens.

The reporter noted that the AI solved a tricky Korean question in one second, which was 300 times faster than them. They stated that detection of cheating would be harder if a user practiced controls or used the device selectively. The reporter observed that the battery drained from 75 percent to 30 percent during the 20 minute math session. They mentioned that head movements and touching the temple might look suspicious to a proctor in a real room. The reporter also found that the AI struggled with science inquiry items due to the need for separate training.

Education authorities are preparing to ban AI glasses from test sites to protect the fairness of the national exam. A top scorer in the certified tax accountant exam recently turned themselves in for cheating using an ultra-small camera. Police stated that smart glasses were not among the devices used by that specific individual in the tax exam. Other reported cheating methods include modified calculators, internal vibrating devices, and wireless bone-conduction earphones bitten with a molar. These developments affect the integrity of the CSAT, which is seen as a key gateway in Korean society.

The Human Resources Development Service of Korea detected smart glasses cheating in four of five national technical qualification test cases. Major generative AI models gave conflicting wrong answers to the same Korean question just one year ago. The 2026 CSAT Korean question used in the test had a wrong-answer rate of 77.7 percent among students. The reporter who conducted the test had previously scored in the top tier for Korean during their school days. The reporter had sat the 2021 CSAT in the math Type A track without elective subjects like Calculus.

Authorities cannot deploy radio-frequency or metal detectors to every nationwide test site within the three days before the exam. Professor Choi Kyung-jin of Gachon University said existing proctoring rules make it difficult to detect AI-enabled cheating. He stated that new rules are needed because the advancement of artificial intelligence is an unstoppable tide of the times. The articles leave open how the government will effectively police sophisticated devices with the current proctoring manual. It remains unclear if higher-performance products will be more difficult to detect than the affordable Rokid model.

This individual allegedly used a miniature camera disguised as a shirt button and a smartphone to obtain an average percentile score of 98.6. These claims surfaced shortly after Han Won-seok, the top scorer on this year's tax accountant qualification exam, confessed to using similar AI tools. Han admitted to using a miniature camera and generative AI during both rounds of the national exam in April and July. He scored 397.5 out of 400 points and achieved perfect scores in three of the four subjects.

The current situation requires the Education Ministry to implement strict measures to prevent the use of hidden cameras and smart glasses. YouTuber Kim Min-woo, known as Mimiminu, has urged the government to postpone the upcoming Suneung to ensure proper security. He noted that the exam was previously delayed in 2017 due to the Pohang earthquake and in 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. To combat these threats, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook vowed on Tuesday to root out AI cheating by activating an interagency emergency response team. The government plans to ban smart devices and deploy additional staff at testing sites to maintain the integrity of the process.

Several education experts have expressed deep concern regarding the ability of authorities to detect modern cheating devices. Kim Min-woo explained that tiny devices hidden in bracelets or buttons can solve complex questions very quickly. Kang Sung-tae, the founder of Gongsin.com, argued that checking for thick-framed glasses is insufficient because many smart glasses from China have discreet designs. He stated that he has warned for years that AI-assisted cheating was inevitable and hoped his warnings would raise awareness. These experts believe that the current screening methods are outdated and cannot stop sophisticated technology.

The South Korean government is now racing to curb these technological breaches before the college entrance exam takes place this Thursday. Authorities are focusing on identifying a wide variety of smart glasses and other wearable electronics that students might smuggle into the rooms. The Education Ministry must now decide if the existing laws allow for a schedule change to better prepare for these threats. If the government cannot guarantee a fair environment, the pressure to delay the exam may increase. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI cheating confession puts Korea’s exams under scrutiny ahead of CSAT
stories.Summary:
A 34-year-old man surnamed Han admitted to using generative AI to cheat on the 2026 national tax accountant qualification exam. He turned himself in to police on Sunday and posted an apology video on YouTube on November 15. Han used AI smart glasses and a micro camera to send exam questions to a smartphone for answers. This confession prompted the presidential office to order a sweeping review of suspected AI cheating cases. The incident occurred just days before the national college entrance exam, known as the CSAT.

The review covers 528 national exams and includes the 63rd national tax accountant qualification exam where Han scored 100 in three subjects. Han earned 97.5 in public finance, while the 16,856 tax law test takers averaged 30.18 with no others above 90. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency assigned the case to the public crime investigation team for potential business obstruction. Under Article 314 of the Criminal Act, Han faces up to five years in prison or 15 million won. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea, or HRDK, will revoke his score and file a complaint.

Ha Joon-kyung, the presidential director of national policy, convened an emergency meeting on Sunday to address the cheating. Ha stated that the Ministry of Education and other agencies must examine every possibility to prevent AI cheating. The HRDK said it would consider using radio frequency detectors and proctors dedicated to checking for AI devices. The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants will launch a new evaluation system during practical training for apprentices. This system aims to screen out individuals who passed professional licensing exams by using cheating methods.

One tax accountant candidate called for a retest because the fairness of the exam had completely collapsed. A test taker surnamed Lee, who earned perfect LEET scores, faced online suspicion due to poor past CSAT grades. Lee previously took the CSAT five times starting in 2013 and once received a grade 7 in Korean. Other suspicions targeted three Yonsei University Mirae Campus dental hygiene graduates and candidates of the licensed customs broker exam. Suspicions also reached the certified appraiser, grade-5 national civil service, and Medical and Dental Education Eligibility tests.

Six cases of AI smart glasses cheating were caught through October in exams for gas craftsmen and various engineers. Cheating was also found in the financial investment analyst exam, the LEET, and university essay exams for early admission. Three Toeic takers and one TEPS taker were caught using AI, as were some middle and high school students. Equipment like 50,000-won micro cameras and 10,000-won earpieces are easily bought on overseas sites, including new AI pens. Critics say lax proctoring and a lack of rules on AI cheating contributed to these widespread problems.

The Education Ministry banned AI smart glasses on the CSAT, meaning violators will be barred for one year. Radio frequency detectors and revised enforcement rules banning smart glasses are not expected until the 2027 college entrance exam. The HRDK formed a task force in August and deployed 327 AI inspectors across two national qualification exams. Professor Choi Byoung-ho noted that Korea has virtually no AI cheating rules and requires a considerable budget for equipment. Professor Kim Byeong-chan suggested changing exam questions to evaluate the thought process rather than just the final result.

stories.Headline: South Korea pushes a health data law that lets researchers use pseudonymized medical records without patient consent
stories.Summary:
The government is pushing the Digital Healthcare Act, which would let pseudonymized medical information be used broadly without individual consent to promote medical AI development and health research, and the plan has sparked controversy. The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the National Assembly are seeking to enact the law, with passage targeted within the year, according to the 16th report. The Lee Jae Myung government had presented as a national agenda the building of an AI expressway to leap into the top three AI powers. It stated that in the bio and healthcare sectors the government would collect and link data to create a data ecosystem. Critics say the bill lowers the threshold for data use without adequate personal information safeguards.

The core of the bill is to establish a legal basis for the secondary use of personal health and medical information and to build large-scale datasets on that basis. At present, pseudonymized medical data can be used for research when individuals are hard to identify, but data collection is restricted and external transfer must be approved by the medical institutions holding the data. Under the bill, the Minister of Health and Welfare may request data provision from the National Health Insurance Service, the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service, medical data-centered hospitals and participating medical institutions. Absent special reasons, institutions that receive requests must comply. For example, if the ministry requests from Hospital A the clinical information of patients who underwent cancer surgery in a given year, the hospital must provide it in pseudonymized form unless there are special reasons not to.

A Ministry of Health and Welfare official explained that a researcher who wishes to use health and medical data must undergo review at each individual institution. The official said review criteria and procedures differ across institutions, so it often takes more than a year just to collect the data. The official also said the government has no authority to oversee whether the reviews are being conducted properly. Lee Sang-yun, chief research fellow at Research Community Health and Alternatives and an occupational and environmental medicine specialist, said that if his medical information were to be used to advance the AI industry, many people would likely not agree. He said there is currently no consent process in place that ensures individual autonomy.

Civil society groups, labor circles and patient organizations are demanding supplements, saying protections for patient rights and personal information are lacking compared with the industrial use of medical information. The data provided may include genetic information or whether the patient has a rare disease, which can allow inferences about the patient and the family disease history. Information on rare diseases with only a few dozen patients may, when combined with other information, identify an individual. Kim Sung-Ju, head of the Korea Severe Disease Alliance, said at a National Assembly forum held on the 2nd that if research achievements based on patient information come back as high-priced pharmaceuticals or treatment technologies, the costs will again be borne by patients and the public. The current bill does not specify a right for individuals to refuse the provision of their information.

The UK and Germany institutionally guarantee a patient's right not to agree to the use of their health and medical information for research and similar purposes. In England, the National Health Service operates a National Data Opt-out system that allows patients to refuse the use of their medical information for research, policymaking and similar uses. Patients can register or withdraw their refusal at any time via the website or by phone. Another issue raised is that even if particular researchers or companies obtain industrial benefits from research using medical information, there is no structure that allows the patients who provided the information or the public to share in those benefits. The article was translated by an AI tool.

More to follow.

Articles.Title: ‘AI development’ will use medical data… patients have no way to refuse

stories.Headline: Anthropic ranks Japan 32nd for per capita Claude use as it seeks 3.5 billion dollars from Japanese investors
stories.Summary:
Anthropic released its Economic Index on November 16, 2026, to measure the global adoption of its artificial intelligence tool, Claude. The data reveals that Japan currently ranks 32nd among 121 different countries and regions regarding per capita usage of the software. This specific ranking suggests that the adoption of artificial intelligence in Japan lags behind its peers in the G7. The low uptake is particularly evident in sectors of the Japanese economy that are currently starved for labor.

The company is now preparing for a massive initial public offering to expand its reach and capabilities. As part of this financial move, Anthropic seeks to raise up to 3.5 billion dollars from investors based in Japan. This push for capital comes as the Japanese government asks both Anthropic and OpenAI for increased access to their most advanced models. Such access is seen as a necessary step to improve national productivity within a shrinking population.

The report highlights a critical need for better integration of these tools to combat labor shortages. While the specific spokespeople were not quoted, the index indicates that Japan must accelerate its AI implementation to remain competitive. The broader context involves an insatiable global demand for chips and a growing talent shortage that bottlenecks expansion. Future developments will depend on whether Japanese investors provide the requested funding and if the government secures better model access.

stories.Headline: Kotozna secures two Japanese patents for conversational AI on its 10th anniversary
stories.Summary:
Kotozna Inc., a Tokyo-based B2B SaaS company led by CEO Genri Goto, announced on November 17, 2026, that it had secured two Japanese patents for its conversational AI technology. The announcement coincided with the company's 10th anniversary, marking a decade of work in multilingual communication and enterprise AI. Kotozna was founded in October 2016 with a mission to overcome language barriers, and it has since expanded from multilingual communication services to generative AI-powered digital concierges, enterprise chatbots and interactive AI avatars. Its solutions now provide customer assistance around the clock in more than 50 languages, which reduces repetitive staff inquiries.

The two patents are JP 7898212, called a Prompt Creation System, and JP 7932206, called an Answer Generation System, and together they cover prompt optimization and knowledge retrieval. Rather than sending large amounts of information to AI models for every question, the technology builds optimized prompts containing only the information needed to generate appropriate responses. Unlike conventional RAG systems that divide documents into fixed-length segments, Kotozna's approach organizes information into meaningful sections so that important context is preserved. The company says this reduces unnecessary processing and token consumption, which helps improve response accuracy, lower latency and optimize AI operating costs, while also supporting efficient knowledge base updates as information changes.

Goto said the mission over the past ten years had stayed the same, which is to make communication easier through technology. He described the patents as an important milestone in the company's journey and as a reflection of its commitment to developing AI that is innovative, reliable and practical for businesses worldwide. The company states that its technology addresses three critical challenges in enterprise AI adoption, namely accuracy, speed and cost efficiency, enabling businesses to deploy reliable and scalable conversational AI solutions. Kotozna's solutions are deployed at more than 500 hotels and over 50 facilities and organizations, including airports, tourism organizations, shopping malls and public institutions in Japan and overseas.

As Kotozna enters its second decade, the company says it will continue advancing its conversational AI capabilities toward intelligent AI agents that can handle complex inquiries, execute tasks and automate customer service workflows. It aims to strengthen its global presence through new deployments and partnerships, bringing its AI solutions to more businesses in hospitality, tourism, retail and other sectors worldwide. Kotozna reported capital of 70,000,000 yen as of December 31, 2025, and its head office is on the third floor of Hulic JP Akasaka in Minato-ku, Tokyo.

stories.Headline: Japan defense minister Shinjiro Koizumi plans AI guidelines for military use by end of November 2026
stories.Summary:
Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced plans on Sunday, November 16, 2026, to issue new guidelines for artificial intelligence. These rules will govern how the Defense Ministry and Self-Defense Forces personnel utilize this technology. The government intends to release the official documents by the end of November 2026. This initiative was unveiled during a visit to Yokosuka in Kanagawa Prefecture.

The new guidelines will require an update to the basic AI policy that was originally compiled in July 2024. These rules will focus on three pillars, including the requirement that humans make all final decisions and accept responsibility for the results. The framework also aims to transform data into a defensive power for the nation. Finally, the ministry seeks to balance the fast spread of AI with the need for enhanced safety.

Minister Koizumi is responsible for this shift and told reporters that the government will not hesitate to revise policies. He explained that revisions are necessary because the field of artificial intelligence changes very rapidly. The minister stated that the government wants to show a new direction for national security. He believes that utilizing AI and data will strengthen the overall defense capabilities of the country.

stories.Headline: OpenAI launches a science blog for researchers to share AI discoveries
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 15, 2026 that it is starting a science blog meant to give scientists and academic researchers a place to share what they are discovering with AI and how they are doing the work. The company said its mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity, and that accelerating scientific discovery is one of the most impactful ways it can work toward that goal. The blog will publish work across a broad range of scientific disciplines, including new scientific results and updates on ongoing research from OpenAI, its collaborators, and the broader scientific community. It will also share methods and practical guidance, such as how scientists use OpenAI models for scientific computing, data analysis, exploring literature, and planning experiments, including how to check the work and where a method falls short. The blog will further carry firsthand accounts from researchers using AI, what they are learning, and how these capabilities are affecting their disciplines, along with discussion of open questions about scientific practice.

The announcement cited several recent results from OpenAI. In September, an internal OpenAI system produced a proof addressing the Navier, Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a longstanding question about the equations describing fluid motion. In early October, the company released a broad range of mathematical results, among them a result on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis that sharpens estimates of how many prime numbers lie below a given number. Later that month, it shared results across mathematics, computer science, and physics concerning how waves concentrate, the limits of efficient computation, and the mathematical foundations of interlacing quantum field theory. In biology, OpenAI said researchers are using AI to analyze complex datasets, connect findings across fields, and develop new hypotheses to test in the lab.

Working with PerturbAI and Scripps Research, thousands of agents powered by GPT-Rosalind analyzed existing experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells in 32 minutes, according to the announcement. By connecting the effects of gene disruptions with scientific literature, the agents identified possible biological mechanisms for scientists to test. OpenAI also said César de la Fuente’s team uses ChatGPT and Codex to build algorithms that identify potential antibiotic molecules, which the team then makes and tests in the lab. The company said these capabilities bring new possibilities and changes to scientific practice, and that in mathematics, systems that generate proofs raise questions about how new arguments are checked, explained, and incorporated into the field.

OpenAI said that in experimental sciences, exploring more hypotheses creates opportunities and challenges in deciding which experiments to pursue, and that across disciplines researchers are considering what these tools mean for training, attribution, and the skills their work requires. The company said the implications will differ by field, and that scientific communities should help shape how these tools are used. OpenAI said it hopes the blog helps more people understand how AI is changing science and how they can use it to explore new questions and make discoveries of their own. The announcement did not say what the blog’s first posts will be or when they will appear.

stories.Headline: Bland releases Tofu-1, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model for phone calls
stories.Summary:
Bland, the San Francisco voice-AI company, released Tofu-1, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model in research preview, according to a MarkTechPost report dated November 15, 2026. The model is built for phone calls from moving cars, hospital rooms and weak-signal lines, and it listens while it speaks and reasons while it talks. For phone-agent teams, one model now handles audio in and audio out with no transcript in between. Tofu-1 is the first release in a planned family of Bland speech-to-speech models, and Bland has not published the internal architecture.

Most voice agents are cascades that turn speech into text, pass it to a language model and turn the reply back into speech, but Tofu-1 listens to audio directly so tone, hesitation and background sound stay available to the model. Bland lists speaker tracking, which tells speakers apart and works out who each one is addressing, and noise separation, which separates voices from a crying child, a TV, highway traffic, a hospital intercom or keypad tones. It also hears paralinguistics such as hesitation, frustration and urgency, and callers can interrupt or correct it mid-sentence while it keeps the conversation moving and reports a result only when the work is done. Because it models the sound of a call, it can also produce one, including a second speaker, the room around them and line noise.

Bland describes a TV Test that asks whether the model can follow the caller while ignoring speech from another scene, and the company marks its walkthrough as illustrative rather than recorded model output. Research preview access is open to a limited number of enterprises, with banking, healthcare, insurance and government named as target sectors, and the sign-up form asks for monthly call volume from under 1,000 to 50,000+. The only number Bland reports is that over 92% could not spot it in screenings, and there is no size, latency, pricing or benchmark data yet, while rivals publish latency and tool-use scores. Access is a closed enterprise preview, with Bland citing January availability.

stories.Headline: Terray and NVIDIA fine-tune Nemotron models to extract chemical reaction data from papers
stories.Summary:
Terray Therapeutics, an AI pharmaceutical company founded in 2018, announced in October 2026 progress in its cooperation with NVIDIA on fine-tuning the Nemotron series vision-language models. The two parties fine-tuned the models to extract molecular structures, reactants and synthetic routes from chemical reaction diagrams in scientific papers. In the RxnCaption benchmark test, the model's HybridMatch F1 score increased from 59.8 to 63.4. The article states this progress does not mean the laboratory's synthesis efficiency improved. It reflects that the model's ability to identify and extract chemical reaction information was enhanced, providing more available data for subsequent synthetic route planning.

In November 2025, Terray named its system EMMI, a small molecule R&D platform connecting experimental hardware, automated workflows and multiple AI modules. Terray independently developed an ultra-high-density microarray chip to fix a large number of small molecules on the chip and measure their binding to target proteins in parallel. As of June 2026, Terray disclosed it had completed more than 420 billion individual measurements in total, involving more than 17 billion unique target-molecule interactions. Terray launched TerraSynth in June 2026, and in 17 internal projects the molecules proposed using this workflow are about 2 to 4 times faster in synthesis than design schemes not considering synthesis constraints, with synthesis delay reduced by up to 75%. On a single NVIDIA A6000 GPU, TerraBind-Struct's end-to-end inference speed for a single protein-ligand complex is about 26 times that of Boltz-2, and on the public CASP16 test set and the company's internal dataset its Pearson correlation coefficient is about 16% to 20% higher than Boltz-2.

In February 2026, CEO Jacob Berlin said in an interview with GEN that the company's fastest advancing self-developed project is a brain-penetrant inhibitor for multiple sclerosis, expected to enter the clinic in 2027. The interview did not disclose specific targets and preclinical data. In 2024, Terray expected its first candidate drug to enter the clinic in 2026, and by February 2026 this timeline was updated to 2027. In December 2025, Terray announced it had reached the first drug discovery milestone in its cooperation with BMS, saying the results involved challenging targets that previously lacked chemical starting points. The company did not disclose the specific target, candidate molecule, project stage or milestone amount.

In its cooperation with Gilead, the two parties carry out small molecule drug discovery and development around multiple targets, and if Gilead exercises its exclusive license option it will be responsible for subsequent development and commercialization of related compounds. Terray will be eligible to receive upfront payments, R&D and sales milestone payments, and sales royalties. In these cooperations, pharmaceutical companies mainly provide target resources and related disease biology knowledge, while Terray relies on its own high-throughput experiments and AI platform to carry out small molecule drug discovery. Recursion takes cellular phenotypic data as an important entry point, observing through automated cell experiments, high-content imaging and multi-omics analysis how cell states change after gene or compound perturbation. The article states that not all AI pharmaceutical companies take building their own laboratories as the core of platform construction, and even if they all invest in experimental capabilities, the data produced by each company is different.

The article states that AI can generate tens of thousands of molecules in an instant, but producing them still requires a large amount of time and experimental resources. It states that molecular design and computational screening are continuously accelerating, yet experimental capabilities do not necessarily grow in sync. Public databases have accumulated a large number of molecular structures and experimental results, but there are differences in detection methods, experimental conditions and data accuracy among different laboratories, and coverage of non-hit molecules is insufficient. For targets lacking known active molecules and not fully studied, it is often difficult to obtain sufficient training information relying only on public data. The article states that models can propose tens of thousands of designs, but the number of molecules laboratories can synthesize and test is limited, and the highest prediction score does not necessarily mean the molecule is most worthy of investing experimental resources.

The article states that whether Terray's platform can be truly transformed into drug assets still needs more project results to answer. It states that the platform continues to expand and cooperations are continuously advancing, but the self-developed pipeline is still in the preclinical stage. The article states that phased milestones in pharmaceutical company cooperation can reflect the application value of the platform in specific projects, but self-developed drugs still have to go through candidate identification, preclinical research and clinical trials. It states that a one-year difference is hardly a breach of promise, but shows that platform capabilities and clinical progress are two different curves. The article states that whether the technical system is effective ultimately needs to be answered by R&D projects.

stories.Headline: Claroc finds 37,571 Grok apps online and 94.7% open without login
stories.Summary:
Security firm Claroc discovered that more than 35,000 applications built with Grok are accessible without login, and some expose corporate confidential information and personal privacy data. Claroc tested 43,551 Grok Build application addresses, of which 37,571 are still online, and found that 94.7% of the online applications can be opened without logging in. Claroc estimates that about 650 to 800 of these applications contain private data. The affected parties include SpaceXSI, the merged entity of SpaceX and xAI owned by Elon Musk, and X. Tesla, which has not been merged with those entities, also did not escape the leak.

The involved institutions include SpaceXSI, X, and 30 other enterprises, 6 of which are listed in the Fortune 500. A Tesla service center scorecard posted the names, work efficiency and bonus details of 22 technicians on a public web page. A brief for ICU patients included patients' laboratory test results, imaging examination records and ventilator usage status. A contractor's working hour management application wrote the plaintext passwords of 18 accounts into the script, and anyone who visits the page can download the data. SpaceXSI's internal sales tool contained strategic customer accounts, sales business opportunities and internal team information.

SpaceXSI told the media that all applications are private before the creator actively shares them, and publishing an application requires multiple steps. The company also stated that its employee accounts are set to "Only you" by default, and users need to actively modify the permissions to make the application public. Claroc said that in its paid accounts used for testing, the pre-selected option on the publishing panel is "Anyone with the link". Claroc said being private before publication and who is allowed to access the application by default when publishing are two completely separate issues. Claroc said that even if you confirm multiple times, the system will not automatically add a list of team members to the access permission list.

Some people on X think that it is the users themselves who opened the permission incorrectly, while others think that Grok's default permission setting is problematic. Claroc used fictional data to build a customer management application for a four-person sales team on its own. The researchers found that the application adds the visitor to the team first, and then checks whether he is a team member. The researchers logged in with a Google account that had never been invited, and they not only saw all the customer data, but also successfully modified one record and deleted another. Claroc conducted a control test on ChatGPT applications, whose sharing panel is set to "Only me" by default, so even if others find the URL, they cannot access it.

When you use Grok vibecoding, it assigns a unique URL to each published application, in the form of random-name.grok.me. These random names are composed of several words, and the original design intention is to make them difficult for others to guess. Claroc found that these application addresses can be found in batches through Passive DNS databases. Every time someone visits a website, the computer queries the server address corresponding to the domain name through DNS, and some DNS resolution services collect these query records and store them in a searchable database. If the access permission of the application is set to "Anyone with the link", then anyone who finds the URL can open it directly.

After switching to the "Only you" mode, strangers will be denied access to the page and data interface, and unpublishing can also take the application offline within a few seconds. SpaceXSI did not start removing the relevant links until several hours after Ars Technica sent the interview email. As of the release of the report, all 24 applications created by SpaceXSI and X employees have been taken offline. A large number of applications created by other users are still accessible, and Claroc has begun to contact the affected institutions on its own. Ars Technica has not yet received a clear response on whether the platform will actively notify other affected customers.

stories.Headline: Google launches two specialized TPU chips and challenges NVIDIA's general-purpose roadmap
stories.Summary:
Google released two new TPU chips, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max, according to a 36Kr article dated 13 November 2026. Google designed the chips itself, and the article said the launch challenged NVIDIA's general-purpose chip roadmap. The 8tx is sold to government agencies and regulated industries and features chip-level data encryption. The 8i Max packages two chips in the same enclosure and focuses on ultra-long context processing. Amin Vahdat, head of Google's chip business, told Bloomberg that "the future belongs to specialization."

Google usually launched a new AI processor every two years, but that rhythm was disrupted in 2026. Vahdat said four TPU products will each be optimized for different needs. The 8tx works with AMD CPUs to encrypt data at the chip level, bypassing the usual step of decrypting data in memory before processing. The 8i Max integrates two TPUs in the same package, raising both computing power and memory capacity. Vahdat said that capability matters for drug R&D and mathematical computing and is also critical for programming applications.

Vahdat said Google could build one general-purpose chip for the whole market or launch different specialized versions, and that the latter approach lets it "actually create more value for our customers." He said the 8tx lets data be processed without first being decrypted in memory, part of Google's cooperation with AMD. He said the 8i Max's combined computing power and memory are important for drug R&D, mathematical computing and programming. He also said the TPU team gets early access to Google's latest Gemini model, which is used to improve chip energy efficiency and detect software vulnerabilities. He said AI is reducing the probability of design flaws that can cause billions of dollars in losses.

Oracle's senior vice president of cloud infrastructure, Karan Batta, said that as AI workloads become increasingly complex, customers need more choices. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Mandeep Singh said TPUs cost about 30% less than NVIDIA GPUs while remaining competitive in throughput, though Google's TPU business margin is not that high. Counterpoint Research vice president Neil Shah said developers' time, code and project experience in CUDA are sunk costs that cannot be migrated. Jump Trading chief technology officer Alex Davies said the firm has thousands of TPUs, mainly to train models assisting trading research, but still mainly uses NVIDIA chips for model training, and only a small number of employees are particularly fond of TPUs.

Google TPUs have attracted Apple, Meta and Oracle, and in October Oracle announced that from next year its cloud customers could use Google TPUs for the first time, where they could previously choose only NVIDIA and AMD products. According to a recent regulatory filing, Anthropic has an option to buy up to $150 billion worth of TPUs between 2028 and 2031, and Bloomberg previously reported that OpenAI also plans to buy TPUs. Google wrote in its financial report that all currently available TPUs have already been booked by customers. Google cooperates with Broadcom on chip design and production coordination, signed an agreement with Broadcom competitor Marvell in recent months, and MediaTek is reported to be supporting the TPU business. A startup called Tenspresso, founded by two former TPU engineers, is developing its first chip aimed directly at the 8i Max's market, with design at least another year from completion.

Bloomberg Intelligence estimates that by 2028 Google's TPU-related sales of chips, software and hardware will exceed $135 billion, against an expected $12 billion this year, a figure that excludes revenue from customers using TPUs through Google Cloud. The same research says opposition to data center construction may cut the $1.4 trillion tech companies expected to invest in 2027 by 5% to 7%, spending that covers chips, network equipment, land and other materials. The article said market concerns about a possible slowdown in AI infrastructure investment are weighing on tech stocks, and the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections has brought new uncertainties to data center projects. More than a decade ago Google developed TPUs to reduce its purchases of NVIDIA GPUs. The article said the competition is not about whose chips are faster but about who can make developers modify fewer lines of code.

stories.Headline: KAIST researchers led by Ro Yong-man develop AI that reads lips without sound to convert speech into text
stories.Summary:
Researchers at KAIST developed an artificial intelligence system that reads lip movements without sound on Sunday, November 15, 2026. A team led by Professor Ro Yong-man of the School of Electrical Engineering created this technology to convert visible speech into text. The system uses a diffusion large language model to identify clear words first and then interprets ambiguous ones using surrounding context. This approach allows the AI to overcome visual ambiguity by placing recognizable pieces of a sentence like a puzzle.

The framework, called DLLM-VSR, achieved a word error rate of 19.4 percent using the LRS3 dataset which contains 433 hours of video. This result was the lowest among methods trained solely with that specific labeled dataset. The researchers also implemented a two-stage training method to align lip movements with text and predict sentence lengths. This work received an Outstanding Paper Award at the EMNLP 2026 international conference on natural language processing. The project was supported by the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation and the 2026 Jang Young-sil Fellowship Program.

Professor Ro Yong-man, the corresponding author, stated that flexible word generation helps solve the fundamental challenges of visual speech recognition. He explained that the team hopes this technology will provide a foundation for physical AI systems used in industrial settings and everyday life. Postdoctoral researcher Yeo Jeong-hun served as the first author, while doctoral researchers Kim Chae-won and Rha Hyeong-seop acted as co-authors. They believe the system could eventually be integrated into communication aids for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The technology may also be useful in noisy industrial environments where traditional speech recognition fails to distinguish voices from background noise. Because the system has only been tested on research datasets, its effectiveness in clinical settings or daily conversations remains unproven. The team now plans to reduce the computational requirements and the size of the model. This will allow the AI to operate in real time on robots or wearable devices without needing an internet connection.

stories.Headline: KAIST team led by Noh Yong-man develops lip-reading AI that cuts word error rate to 19.4%
stories.Summary:
KAIST announced on the 15th that a research team led by Professor Noh Yong-man of the School of Electrical Engineering developed a technology improving the accuracy of visual speech recognition, which converts spoken words into text by analyzing lip movements. The team used a diffusion large language model, which repeatedly fills in blanks in a sentence, to decode ambiguous lip movements by leveraging surrounding context. Conventional AI models generate sentences sequentially from the first word, so an incorrect word at the beginning propagates errors through the rest of the sentence. The team changed this approach from reading in order from the beginning to reading from the most certain parts first. The system first identifies words whose lip movements are clearly distinguishable, then uses those words as clues to decode the remaining parts.

The team trained the AI on the 433-hour lip-reading video dataset LRS3, and it achieved a word error rate of 19.4%, the lowest error rate reported among previous studies using LRS3 as a training dataset with reference sentences provided. Word error rate is the proportion of words incorrectly recognized, omitted, or unnecessarily added when the AI's output is compared with the reference sentence. The team split AI learning into two stages, teaching it to associate lip movements in the video with corresponding text content and to model sentence length. When decoding speech, the AI estimated several possible sentence lengths based on video duration and selected the most reliable sentence.

The team received the Outstanding Paper Award at the international conference Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing 2026. Professor Noh said the study is significant in that it demonstrates how flexibly controlling the order in which AI generates words alone can overcome fundamental limitations of speech recognition with visual ambiguity. He said the team aims to establish a reliable physical AI foundation that can be used across diverse devices in everyday life and industrial settings. Postdoctoral Researcher Yeo Jeong-hoon is the first author.

Humans find it difficult to understand speech using only lip movements without hearing the sound, because there are words whose sounds differ but whose lip movements look similar. The research team's approach is similar to solving a puzzle by first fitting the pieces with clear shapes and then filling in the surrounding pieces. The technology is expected to be used as a communication tool, such as converting speech to text in noisy environments or supporting communication for people who are deaf or hard of hearing. It could be developed into devices that understand workers' speech in noisy industrial sites or assist conversations among people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The research team plans to reduce the size and computational cost of the AI model so it can be deployed on various devices. Enabling real-time AI operation on wearable devices or robots without an internet connection is their next challenge. The articles do not state when the research began or how long the project took. More to follow.

The training involved two stages to link lip movements with text and to learn various sentence lengths. During testing with a public evaluation dataset of 433 hours of video, the technology recorded a word error rate of 19.4%. stories.Summary:
A research team from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a technology to improve visual speech recognition on November 15, 2026. Led by Professor Noh Yong-man of the School of Electrical Engineering, the team created a system that converts lip movements into text more accurately. This new method addresses the common problem where different sounds produce similar lip shapes, which often confuses traditional artificial intelligence. By utilizing a diffusion large language model, the system can now decode ambiguous movements by analyzing the surrounding context of a sentence.

The technology changes the processing order by identifying the most certain words first rather than reading tokens sequentially from the beginning. This approach allows the AI to use clear lip movements as clues to fill in the remaining blanks in a sentence. During a proof-of-concept test using 433 hours of video, the team achieved a word error rate of 19.4 percent. This system is designed to support assistive communication in environments where audio is difficult to hear, making speech more accessible.

Professor Noh stated that flexibly controlling the word generation order allows the AI to overcome the fundamental limits of visual ambiguity. He believes this work establishes a foundation for using trusted speech recognition across various industrial settings and everyday devices. Separately, KAIST is partnering with Nvidia to develop sovereign AI optimized for the Korean language under the leadership of Professor Kim Hyun-woo. Kim noted that South Korea lacks the massive training datasets available to English or Chinese markets, which can undermine the quality of local AI responses.

The joint KAIST and Nvidia laboratory aims to create one million high-quality Korean data samples for public release by the end of 2027. These datasets and training methodologies will be provided free of charge to help domestic companies reduce development costs. The researchers plan to generate synthetic materials and select high-quality examples to bridge the existing data gap. stories.Headline: Algernon Yau warns Hong Kong to prepare for a potential global AI slowdown
stories.Summary:
Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau warned on Sunday, November 15, 2026, that the global development of artificial intelligence might experience a slowdown. This caution follows a period of significant economic growth, as Hong Kong exports surged by nearly 65 percent in September compared to the previous year. This increase represents the fastest monthly year-on-year growth the city has seen in more than four decades. Yau believes the region must remain vigilant because the current upward trend is heavily driven by AI advancements.

To maintain its status as an international trade centre, Hong Kong must adjust its strategies and expand its trade network. The city needs to pay close attention to global trends because different countries hold varying views on how AI should advance. These external influences could cause the current boom to subside, requiring the SAR to seek new opportunities. Yau also mentioned the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen as a way to build a regional community.

Speaking on a Commercial Radio programme, Yau explained that the global landscape is constantly evolving and subject to external pressures. He stated that the nation hopes economies within the Asia-Pacific region can cooperate to achieve mutual development. The minister emphasized that the city must be prepared for shifts in technology to ensure long-term economic stability. By monitoring international trends, Hong Kong can better navigate the potential decline of the artificial intelligence boom.

stories.Headline: Nvidia investigates Jensen Huang after allegations of ties to Chinese intelligence agent
stories.Summary:
Allegations emerged on November 11, 2026, that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang. This woman was a former executive at the Singaporean cloud computing firm Megaspeed and is reportedly linked to intelligence services in Beijing. The scandal has prompted the board of Nvidia to investigate if their leader was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Meanwhile, Singapore police are investigating Megaspeed for suspected breaches of domestic laws regarding the illegal transfer of restricted technology.

The situation may require the United States to implement tougher enforcement of export restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips. Washington might focus more closely on neocloud companies in Southeast Asia, specifically in trading hubs like Singapore and Malaysia. This follows a recent case where four individuals and four companies in Singapore faced fraud charges over servers shipped to Malaysia. Additionally, Malaysian customs seized 30 servers containing advanced AI chips worth about 12.1 million US dollars last month.

Alex Capri from the National University of Singapore Business School believes a major crackdown on cloud computing companies is coming. He stated that these services have acted as a loophole allowing global companies to rent computing power without buying chips. Jay Goldberg of Seaport Research Partners suggested that rivals like AMD, Broadcom, and Huawei could benefit from this fallout. He noted that AMD and Broadcom have relatively limited exposure to China compared to the current market leader.

The United States and China remain at odds over critical technologies and the movement of sensitive semiconductors. While the US eased some licensing policies in January, Beijing still requires approval for Nvidia chip imports to promote domestic alternatives. Capri believes this scandal will serve as fuel for the fire regarding China's push for chip self-sufficiency. Nvidia shares fell more than 5 per cent on Tuesday as the company faces this period of leadership uncertainty.

stories.Headline: Applied Materials forecasts first-quarter revenue above estimates due to AI chip demand
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials announced on November 12 that its fiscal first-quarter revenue is expected to exceed Wall Street estimates. This growth is driven by chipmakers who are increasing their spending to meet the massive demand for artificial intelligence chips and memory. The company reported that its fourth-quarter adjusted profit reached US$4.16 per share, which surpassed the average analyst prediction of US$4.05. Its stock has already increased by approximately 48% throughout 2026 as a result of these market trends.

The company forecasts fiscal first-quarter revenue of about US$11.1 billion, plus or minus US$500 million, beating the LSEG estimate of US$10.89 billion. Fourth-quarter Semiconductor Systems revenue rose 64% to US$8 billion, while sales in China grew 35% to US$2.64 billion despite representing 25% of total revenue. Applied Materials is also working with Apple at its Austin, Texas, facility to increase the domestic production of chipmaking equipment. These figures highlight a significant surge in the acquisition of tools for wafer fabrication processes.

Chief executive Gary Dickerson stated that 2027 could be another record year for both the company and the broader market. He noted that demand for wafer fab equipment should rise by more than 30% and that customers are requesting tools sooner. Bob O’Donnell, the chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, observed that current market metrics show demand remains very strong. He added that foundries and chipmakers are currently purchasing as much equipment as they possibly can to keep up.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandals and suspected spying
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on November 12, 2026, following a series of personal and professional scandals. He stepped down as the list of his inappropriate romantic relationships grew, creating a volatile situation for the company. This event occurred within a broader period of turmoil for the artificial intelligence trade during a wild couple of weeks. The resignation followed a barrage of negative headlines and a significant loss in the company's overall market value.

The company, which was the first to reach a value of 5 trillion US dollars, lost 500 billion US dollars in one week. The stock experienced a brutal 14 per cent drop at the open on November 12 before closing down 4 per cent. Nvidia's stock is now trading at a price to forward earnings ratio of around 11 after a 15 per cent swoon this year. These figures are roughly in line with the UK's FTSE 100 index, which is often viewed as a repository for old economy dinosaurs.

One person with the inside track told the Financial Times that Huang was viewed as a god to be worshipped within the company. The report suggests it is a mistake to have key personalities in positions of immense power within flat corporate structures. This situation highlights concerns that too much national security and global wealth are perched on the heads of too few billionaires. These leaders are reminded to be fallible mortals, a sentiment echoed by the tech backlash in the US midterm elections.

US retail investors rushed into the market on November 10 and November 12, with the latter day blowing the former out of the water. Vanda Research stated that inflows from these buyers at the market open were around 40 times bigger than usual. The S&P 500 index, where AI and Big Tech account for 35 per cent, is down 4 per cent from its peak last month. Bond markets are also struggling to absorb the massive borrowing companies are undertaking to fund various data centre projects.

The articles describe a high level of concentration in the AI trade, where a small clutch of big stocks holds up markets globally. This concentration is visible in the US and South Korea, though academic literature suggests it only matters if the central concept collapses. The current market environment is caught between the pressure of rising interest rates and the bulletproof nature of AI excitement. Global markets have faced bigger tests since the Covid-19 pandemic and have generally come through those challenges just fine.

Jensen Huang now faces a grilling in Congress over a relationship with a woman suspected by US authorities of being a Chinese asset. The situation could get worse before it gets better, depending on the outcome of these government inquiries and further revelations. It remains open whether the AI trade will maintain its resilience or if the concentration of risk will lead to a collapse. The articles leave the final impact of the spying suspicions and the corporate leadership transition unresolved for the time being.

stories.Headline: Taisei launches a 150 million dollar fund for AI and robotics startups
stories.Summary:
The Japanese construction company Taisei announced on Monday, November 16, 2026, that it is establishing a new investment fund. This 153-year-old firm is dedicating 150 million dollars to support various startups specializing in robotics and artificial intelligence. The company intends to use these technological advancements to find viable workarounds for a shrinking domestic workforce. This strategic move aims to modernize the business by integrating automation into its traditional construction processes.

The fund will be managed by Pegasus Tech Ventures, a firm based in Silicon Valley that serves as the general partner. This partnership will focus on searching for new investments in automation and related fields through the year 2036. Taisei also plans to target startups that provide liquid-cooling infrastructure and high-density power solutions. These specific investments are intended to support the company as it expands its efforts into the construction of AI data centers.

Anis Uzzaman, who serves as the founder and chief executive officer of Pegasus, explained the purpose of the venture. He stated that the primary objective is to transform a traditional construction firm into a leader enabled by robotics and AI. Uzzaman further noted that the fund will help the company secure the necessary infrastructure for modern data centers. Pegasus currently manages over 2 billion dollars in assets and has previously worked with other Japanese companies like Aisin and Japanet Holdings.

This initiative comes as Japanese businesses struggle with chronic labor shortages, rising wages, and a general backlash against foreign workers. These economic pressures, combined with sliding domestic spending, are pushing more companies to adopt robotic solutions. Taisei has already shown interest in this sector by investing last year in a fund run by Met Fund Advisors. That previous investment focused on emerging startups coming out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

stories.Headline: Remy Cointreau uses an AI sales presenter to attract younger Chinese consumers
stories.Summary:
The French spirits maker Remy Cointreau introduced an artificial intelligence sales presenter named Eve about 18 months ago. This virtual host allows the company to recommend cognac and whiskies to Chinese shoppers at any hour, including 3 am. The initiative aims to attract new customers and expand the company's digital reach. It was highlighted during the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai.

The strategy involves a mix of presenters, with humans handling 80 percent of livestreaming and AI managing 20 percent. On October 28, the company reported first-half fiscal 2026-27 sales of 510.9 million euros, or 566.7 million dollars, which is an organic increase of 2.9 percent. Asia-Pacific sales rose 14.3 percent, while second-quarter e-commerce sales grew by more than 30 percent and made up about 30 percent of China sales. Chief Financial Officer Luca Marotta noted that cognac sales in China grew at a high-single-digit rate in the first half.

Sophie Phe, the CEO of Remy Cointreau China, stated that there is very little overlap between the audiences reached by AI and human hosts. She explained that the company has spent over ten years developing e-commerce tools, such as flagship stores on JD and Tmall. Phe noted that Chinese consumers are now drinking better rather than more, prioritizing quality over quantity. She observed that traditional big banquets and business dinners are decreasing in favor of small-group or personal enjoyment.

This shift is occurring as the premium spirits market in China moves away from formal business entertaining. Younger consumers are now more interested in individual preferences and exploring different flavors than following old habits. To adapt, Remy Cointreau is broadening the appeal of its portfolio, which includes Louis XIII, Cointreau, Remy Martin, and Scotch whiskies. The company is focusing on a value strategy rather than a volume strategy to reach these new drinkers.

stories.Headline: SMIC reports profit surge as China accelerates development of independent AI industry
stories.Summary:
Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp reported a 123.4 percent year-on-year increase in net profit for the third quarter of 2026. This financial growth occurred as Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia, sparking debates about American technology policy. These events highlight a broader trend where growing market demand is providing stronger commercial returns for the Chinese semiconductor industry. The domestic AI sector is now operating from a firmer industrial foundation than it possessed several years ago.

The current situation requires Chinese technology companies to adapt their computing systems to a growing range of homegrown processors. SMIC invested 258.4 million dollars into research and development during the third quarter alone to support this transition. Companies such as Huawei and Cambricon are expanding their market presence to create a self-sustaining AI computing ecosystem. This shift reduces the vulnerability of the industry to external restrictions and decreases the overall dependence on American technology.

The Global Times suggests that the resignation of Jensen Huang may weaken the influence of commercial interests in Washington. They argue that national security concerns are now dominating US technology policy over the commercial arguments previously made by chip companies. The publication claims that tightening export controls has actually accelerated Chinese efforts to build an independent AI industry. They believe that further US restrictions could prompt other Asian economies to diversify their supply chains away from American technology.

The US government is reportedly considering requiring permits for global AI chip sales from companies like Nvidia and AMD. Such measures may lead to greater scrutiny for chip and data center industries across Southeast Asia. If these policies are implemented, US chipmakers might be among the first to bear the costs due to intertwined supply chains. China intends to continue gathering pace in AI development regardless of the political tug-of-war in Washington.

stories.Headline: Chinese financial firms shift capital to AI data centers amid property downturn
stories.Summary:
Chinese banks, insurers, and private equity firms are shifting their capital toward artificial intelligence data centers in the north and west during a property downturn. These sprawling computing campuses are rising in arid regions like Zhongwei in Ningxia and Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia alongside renewable energy plants. This investment trend has accelerated since late 2022 as financial institutions seek steady cash flows and large opportunities backed by identifiable customers. One bank branch official estimated that these computing centers could represent one third of planned lending for their branch in 2027.

The infrastructure requires dense GPU clusters and specialized cooling, with a gigawatt project potentially costing 30 billion yuan for infrastructure and over 100 billion yuan for GPUs. Under the 2022 East Data, West Computing initiative, workloads are steered toward eight national computing hubs to utilize abundant renewable energy. In Ulanqab, electricity costs between 0.32 and 0.35 yuan per kWh could save 5 billion yuan per gigawatt year compared to other sites. During the third quarter of 2026, three telecom operators launched over 225 tender projects worth 36.6 billion yuan, while Alibaba saw second quarter capital expenditure rise 75 percent to 67.7 billion yuan.

State owned carriers and internet giants are leading the expansion, with Tencent reporting first half 2026 capital expenditure of 84.7 billion yuan. A consortium led by China Construction Bank provided a 4.68 billion yuan loan for a Range Intelligent center, and China Development Bank gave a 136 million yuan policy loan to Chindata. Investors noted that daily token usage in China grew from 100 billion in early 2024 to over 140 trillion by March 2026. While some believe subsidies help deploy domestic chips, others warn that the probability of another infrastructure glut is not small.

The industry is moving toward more specialized financing, including token loans based on AI activity metrics and the 2025 listing of data center REITs by GDS and Range. IDC projects that global AI investment will reach 815.9 billion dollars by 2028, with China exceeding 100 billion dollars of that total. Future demand is expected to rise as virtual agents and robots emerge and models with 5 trillion parameters require larger clusters. However, some investors remain cautious about tenant concentration and the risk that technical shifts could leave these massive facilities underused.

NTT DATA became a Gold Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, serving as Official AI Consulting Partner and Official Technology Consulting Partner, the company announced on November 12, 2026. The 2026 tournament will take place from November 15 to 22 at Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy. NTT DATA is a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services. The partnership gives NTT DATA a global stage to showcase how AI, data and technology can support human potential. Elite tennis brings together skill, judgment and the ability to adapt under pressure.

NTT DATA will host a Tech Corner in Turin where visitors can see computer vision, Physical AI and advanced AI infrastructure applied to real-world scenarios. Those scenarios include monitoring, safety, construction and humanoid robotics. The space will also house the Mental Economy Gym, powered by Formula Medicine, an Italian company specializing in sports medicine and human performance. Guests there can take on digital challenges that measure indicators such as concentration, reaction and mental workload. At the Fan Village court, NTT DATA will showcase an on-court experience presented by FITP, combining cognitive and physical monitoring with AI-powered computer vision.

Kazuhiko Nakayama, President and CEO of NTT DATA Group, said what makes sport extraordinary is ultimately human, citing the ambition to push boundaries, the courage to take risks and the determination to achieve more. He said technology has the power to unlock even greater possibilities by helping people see what was previously invisible and discover new ways to improve. As an AI Consulting Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, he said, NTT DATA wants to celebrate human potential while demonstrating how technology can expand what people can achieve. He said NTT DATA combines AI capabilities with deep industry expertise to help clients transform their businesses and create new value. The partnership is the latest in a series of sporting partnerships that bring NTT DATA's global brand positioning statement, "Intelligence to Impact," to life.

IT Brief UK reported that the partnership places the technology group alongside one of men's tennis's best-known season-ending events. The report said NTT DATA will use the tournament to show how AI, data and related systems can generate performance insights and support decision-making under pressure. IT Brief UK said the announcement reflects a wider trend in professional sport, where tournaments, teams and governing bodies use technology partnerships to enhance fan experiences and collect more detailed information on athlete preparation and match play. The report said tennis has become a testing ground for data-led analysis, with systems used across officiating, broadcast coverage and training. IT Brief UK said the demonstrations will place tools used in industrial and operational settings into a consumer-facing environment, linking them to measurable human activity rather than back-office processes.

NTT DATA is a $30+ billion business and technology services leader serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. It describes itself as one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA has experts in more than 70 countries. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in R&D. NTT DATA said the partnership reflects its belief that intelligence comes not only from AI and technology, but also from human expertise and deep industry understanding.
