stories.Headline: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
stories.Summary:
OpenAI said on November 16, 2026 that it was sharing new results measuring model performance, safety and cost in clinical and administrative workflows, and that it was working with Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare and CVS Health. The company said computer-use agents carry out multi-step workflows by clicking, typing and moving between applications. OpenAI said healthcare teams, developers and individual clinicians can access these capabilities today through the OpenAI API, ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians. OpenAI said it built a demo using synthetic patient data in which a patient messages a clinician about lower back pain. OpenAI said the agent reviews visit notes, physical therapy records and prior imaging in the EHR, drafts an MRI order, an encounter note and a reply, then prepares a prior authorization request in the insurer's portal.

OpenAI said it evaluated GPT-6 Astra on tasks clinicians handle in their EHR inboxes, shaped by physician input. OpenAI said 99% of 325 reviewed tasks were rated safe, and physicians selected "very helpful" or "extremely helpful" in 93% of 646 assessments on a five-point scale. OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra earned 94.3% of available rubric points on HealthAdminBench, an independent benchmark from Stanford researchers, while GPT-6 Luna earned 91.8% despite costing 98% less at 8.5 cents per task. OpenAI said both models were evaluated at maximum reasoning effort. OpenAI said organizations can support HIPAA-compliant workflows, configure approvals and agent access, and record audit logs, and that organization data is not used to train OpenAI foundation models.

Lagan Khare, Executive Director of Engineering at CVS Health, said less time on administrative work means more time for care and that this is a win for teams and everyone served. Madhu Nutakki, CIO of Cigna Healthcare, said moving from concept to deployment in under eight weeks shows what is possible when AI, care management expertise and the right guardrails come together. Nutakki said it means getting better, more complete insights to case managers sooner so they can focus on supporting patients with personalized, compassionate care. OpenAI said CVS Health uses validation checks and human oversight, with screenshots and action records to verify actions and application state. OpenAI said data remains within CVS Health enterprise-controlled infrastructure, governed by their enterprise AI Governance team and established responsible AI policies, and that production data is not used to train foundation models.

OpenAI said CVS Health is using computer-use capabilities to automate repetitive work across clinical systems, including sending documents, processing referrals and supporting specialist consults. OpenAI said one production workflow cleared a months-long document-sending backlog over a weekend, and another handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consults each day. OpenAI said CVS Health is open sourcing its Agent Kit, built with OpenAI's Agents SDK. OpenAI said Abridge is developing computer-use agents for care plans across applications, including those without APIs, and that its planned inpatient use case builds on the clinical conversation. OpenAI said Cigna Healthcare case managers previously had to navigate more than 10 separate clinical and administrative systems to gather context, and computer use can now bring relevant information together in seconds.

OpenAI said healthcare is fragmented, and teams often need to move information between systems manually before a patient can get care. OpenAI said when a clinician recommends an MRI, the information an insurer needs may be in a patient's medical record, but a team member still needs to retrieve it and enter it into a separate portal to complete an authorization request. OpenAI said its partners build software used in hundreds of health systems, coordinate care for members globally, and deliver care to hundreds of millions of patients. OpenAI said Ambience built additional controls, and that in a demonstration the agent stops and asks the clinician when the record is ambiguous, then waits for approval before submitting. OpenAI said health systems set which actions the agent can take, can pause it at any point, and get a step-by-step log for audit.

OpenAI said healthcare organizations can contact its sales team, and existing customers can ask their workspace administrator to enable computer use in ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI said U.S. clinicians can sign up for a free ChatGPT for Clinicians account today and experience computer use in ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI said developers can build healthcare applications with the OpenAI API and explore its computer use guide. OpenAI said organizations must use eligible services covered by their Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI and the required security and retention settings to support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information. OpenAI said it hopes these advances enable healthcare teams to spend less time moving information through systems and more time caring for patients.

Articles.Title: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams

stories.Headline: LVMH media division and OpenAI sign strategic AI agreement to deploy ChatGPT Enterprise across 17 brands
stories.Summary:
LVMH Group's Media Division and OpenAI announced on 16 November 2026 in Paris that they signed a strategic agreement to support new uses of artificial intelligence across all the division's publications and to make their journalism more accessible through ChatGPT. The agreement covers deployment of OpenAI tools and ChatGPT Enterprise to teams across the media division, which will let them build AI applications tailored to their day-to-day work. The two sides said their shared ambition is to let teams experiment with and develop practical uses of AI that support journalism and high-quality reporting. The partnership also enhances the presence of the division's content in ChatGPT, which will provide summaries and excerpts in response to relevant user questions, identify sources and include direct links to the original articles.

The division, known as Groupe Les Echos-Le Parisien, brings together 17 media brands including Les Echos, Le Parisien, Challenges, Paris Match, L'Opinion, Investir, L'Agefi, Historia, Capital Finance, Connaissance des Arts, Radio Classique, Mezzo and medici.tv. It has 1,800 employees, nearly 700 of them journalists, and reaches more than 27 million people in France every month. Teams will be able to explore applications such as document research, document comparison and preliminary translation, with the stated goal of giving them more time for investigative reporting, analysis and reporting in the field. The partnership is described as a company-wide initiative that will extend across all the division's publications, with training tailored to each person's use cases to support the rollout.

Michèle Benbunan, CEO of LVMH Group's Media Division, said the agreement will position the publications at the forefront of the media industry and that integrating AI will become an everyday asset for all its teams, adding that the division is delighted to work with a partner whose expertise and reputation are recognised worldwide. Emmanuel Marill, Managing Director for EMEA at OpenAI, said quality journalism depends on the people who investigate, verify facts and help audiences make sense of information, and that OpenAI wants to help put AI to work for everyone across the division while respecting editorial independence. He said the aim is to help teams spend more time on what makes their journalism valuable, and that the partnership will give ChatGPT users access to high-quality journalism that keeps pace with the news.

The announcement frames the deal around two pressures on the division's business: newsrooms gaining time for investigation and analysis, and personalisation, which the announcement calls a major priority in an increasingly crowded information landscape. It says AI is an essential tool for developing and delivering products and services that meet the needs of customers, readers and advertisers, helping to attract and retain them and grow revenue across the publications. The announcement also says the partnership will support the evolution of roles throughout the organisation by streamlining operations, improving efficiency and encouraging innovation and creativity. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the rollout and the training.

stories.Headline: PM calls for considering disabling Wi-Fi at CSAT test sites to prevent AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook instructed government officials on Monday, November 16, 2026, to implement strict measures against artificial intelligence cheating. These urgent orders come just three days before the nationwide College Scholastic Ability Test, which is scheduled for this Thursday. The government is reacting to a shocking confession from the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam. This individual admitted on Sunday to using a smartphone, a miniature camera, and generative AI to cheat on two rounds of that test. He further confessed to using these same sophisticated methods to cheat on a certified public accountant exam.

The new requirements involve the education ministry ensuring that all test takers turn in every smart device before the exam begins. Officials must conduct thorough checks to confirm that no smart devices are possessed by students during the testing period. Additionally, the science ministry has been asked to actively consider disabling all public Wi-Fi signals at the test sites. Prime Minister Han also announced the establishment of an interagency emergency response team for the 2027 CSAT to create comprehensive preventive measures. The government intends to investigate any abnormal signs that defy common sense after the exam using objective data.

Prime Minister Han stated that the government must concentrate all national capabilities to prepare against misconduct involving advanced AI technology. She explained that conventional exam management methods are now limited because AI technology is advancing so rapidly. The prime minister emphasized that upholding the fairness of examinations is a fundamental duty directly linked to public trust. She urged each government ministry to develop effective measures and ensure they are implemented thoroughly across all state-administered exams. Han called for the development of advanced detection technologies, including those leveraging AI, to counter ultra-small electronic devices and outside help.

The government is now scrambling to prevent similar AI-assisted cheating from occurring during the upcoming college entrance examinations. This concern follows reports of four separate cheating cases involving AI glasses at middle and high schools earlier this year. Authorities have indicated that they will pursue criminal punishment and a three-year exam ban for any CSAT cheaters using AI glasses. Officials are now tasked with creating a comprehensive government strategy to respond to increasingly diverse and sophisticated methods of cheating. They aim to create a fair testing environment that the public can trust through these new technical measures.

Articles.Title: PM calls for considering disabling Wi-Fi at CSAT test sites to prevent AI cheating

stories.Headline: South Korea and Philippines agree to deepen cooperation in AI and defense industry
stories.Summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. held a summit on Monday, November 16, 2026, in Manila. This meeting occurred on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit and marked the third time the two leaders have met. They previously held discussions in Gyeongju, South Korea, last year and again in the Philippine capital during March. The leaders focused on strengthening ties in traditional sectors and expanding their partnership into several emerging industries.

The agreement requires deeper cooperation in defense manufacturing, infrastructure, shipbuilding, artificial intelligence, nuclear power plants, aerospace, and disaster management. Bilateral trade between the two nations reached US$21.3 billion during the first nine months of this year, which already exceeds the previous annual record. The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on science and technology to expand collaboration into smart farming. Additionally, they signed a grant aid agreement to help the Korea International Cooperation Agency implement various projects in the Philippines.

Spokesperson Kim Sung-wan stated that President Lee requested continued support from the Philippine government to help South Korean companies expand their operations. The spokesperson noted that both leaders pledged to foster mutually beneficial cooperation in areas where their bilateral ties are already strong. President Lee arrived in Manila on Monday for a four-day trip to engage with regional leaders. He is scheduled to travel to Shenzhen, China, next to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

stories.Headline: Anthropic goes public on Thursday in an offering estimated to raise about $64.35 billion
stories.Summary:
Capital Economics wrote on Monday that the AI stock boom is “in its final stages,” and Anthropic is going public on Thursday in a deal estimated to raise about $64.35 billion at the top of its range. That is nearly twice what every U.S. IPO raised together last quarter, according to Renaissance Capital. The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter while employers added an average of 48,000 jobs a month over the 12 months through September, before a 165,000 gain in October. AI spending drove more than half of business-investment growth in the first three quarters of the year, Goldman Sachs estimates. Bloomberg reported on Nov. 12 that the Anthropic deal was about six times oversubscribed, days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO.

J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s David Kelly sees real GDP growth slowing to 1.6% over the next four quarters, with hiring stuck near 50,000 a month. Morgan Stanley’s research digest on Monday, summarizing chief U.S. economist Michael Gapen’s 2027 outlook, put the breakeven at about 50,000 jobs a month.
